p9p8gf.q: On a carriageway of the type shown, you may overtake even on a bend
p9p8gf.why: The carriageway shown has two lanes in each direction; on such carriageways overtaking on a bend is allowed, as long as you stay within your own direction's lanes and never cross the double solid line.

jy9qu7.q: The carriageway of the type shown carries two-way traffic
jy9qu7.why: The picture shows a single carriageway (carreggiata) with two lanes per direction, separated in the middle by a double solid line, so traffic flows in both directions.

10z3r13.q: On an extra-urban carriageway of the type shown, the inner lanes are normally reserved for overtaking
10z3r13.why: On extra-urban carriageways with two lanes per direction, the right lane is for normal driving, while the inner lane next to the double line is normally reserved for overtaking.

1ouwis0.q: On a carriageway of the type shown, U-turns are not allowed
1ouwis0.why: The double solid line in the centre may never be crossed, so a U-turn (inversione di marcia), which would require crossing it, is forbidden.

11potog.q: On an extra-urban carriageway of the type shown, you may overtake on either the right or the left without distinction
11potog.why: Overtaking is normally done on the left; overtaking on the right is allowed only in special cases, such as a vehicle signalling a left turn or a tram in the middle of the road.

mlfkrv.q: On an extra-urban carriageway of the type shown, you may always drive in parallel rows
mlfkrv.why: Outside built-up areas, driving in parallel rows (file parallele) on carriageways with two or more lanes per direction is allowed only when traffic is heavy, not always.

9fb2qm.q: On a carriageway of the type shown, we may start an overtaking manoeuvre even if the driver behind has already started the same manoeuvre
9fb2qm.why: Before overtaking you must check that the driver behind has not already started the same manoeuvre; if they have, you must not overtake and must wait.

brsqpo.q: On the road shown, in each direction, the right lane is normally used for ordinary driving
brsqpo.why: On a carriageway with three lanes per direction, the right-hand lane is for normal driving; the other lanes are normally used for overtaking.

tru98x.q: The road shown has three lanes in each direction
tru98x.why: The picture shows one two-way carriageway, split by a double solid line, with three lanes (corsie) in each direction, six lanes in total.

1j4ju2j.q: On the road shown, in each direction, the centre and left lanes are normally used for overtaking
1j4ju2j.why: With three lanes per direction, the right lane is for normal driving, while the centre and left lanes are normally reserved for overtaking.

4fip7j.q: The road shown consists of one carriageway
4fip7j.why: There is no central reservation: the two directions are separated only by a double solid line, so the road has a single carriageway (carreggiata).

19stggq.q: On the road shown, in each direction, the centre lane is normally used for ordinary driving
19stggq.why: Normal driving takes place in the right lane; the centre lane, like the left lane, is normally used for overtaking.

12hus1b.q: On the road shown, in each direction, the right lane is normally used for overtaking
12hus1b.why: The right lane is for normal driving; overtaking is normally done in the centre and left lanes.

1i5gxqr.q: The road shown consists of two carriageways
1i5gxqr.why: There would be two carriageways only if a central reservation (spartitraffico) separated them; here only a double solid line divides the directions, so it is one carriageway.

wo6hgo.q: On the road shown, in each direction, the left lane is normally used for ordinary driving
wo6hgo.why: The left lane is normally reserved for overtaking; normal driving takes place in the right lane.

3vy9vr.q: The road shown consists of three carriageways
3vy9vr.why: The two green central reservations divide the road into three carriageways: two side ones with two lanes each and a central one with four lanes.

3npfjv.q: The road shown consists of eight lanes
3npfjv.why: There are eight lanes: two in each side carriageway and four in the central one, two per direction.

1ngb7h.q: On the road shown, the side carriageways are normally one-way
1ngb7h.why: The side carriageways, separated by central reservations and with no solid centre line, are normally one-way.

1gjw6bg.q: On the road shown, the central carriageway normally carries two-way traffic
1gjw6bg.why: The central carriageway has four lanes split in half by a double solid line, two lanes for each direction, so it carries two-way traffic.

1z9cyo.q: The road shown normally allows overtaking even on a bend
1z9cyo.why: Every carriageway has at least two lanes per direction; in this case overtaking is allowed even on bends, without entering the opposite direction's lanes.

3wjurd.q: The road shown consists of four carriageways, all one-way
3wjurd.why: There are three carriageways, separated by two central reservations: the two side ones are normally one-way, while the central one is two-way.

konno4.q: The road shown consists of eight carriageways
konno4.why: Eight is the number of lanes (corsie), not carriageways: the carriageways, separated by the central reservations, are three.

1m9ef0b.q: The road shown normally has two carriageways with two-way traffic
1m9ef0b.why: Only the central carriageway is two-way; the two side carriageways are normally one-way.

l2t6be.q: The road shown consists of three lanes
l2t6be.why: Three is the number of carriageways; there are eight lanes: two in each side carriageway and four in the central one.

1xj1pn9.q: On the road shown, the central lane carries two-way traffic
1xj1pn9.why: A lane always carries a single file of vehicles in one direction; no lane is ever two-way. It is the central carriageway that is two-way.

r7mkw5.q: On the side carriageways of the road shown, U-turns are normally allowed
r7mkw5.why: The side carriageways are normally one-way and bounded by central reservations; a U-turn would mean driving against traffic, so it is forbidden.

1a09flf.q: A pedestrian crossing is marked with parallel white stripes
1a09flf.why: A pedestrian crossing is marked by white stripes running parallel to the road's axis, the so-called zebra crossing (zebrature).

1lxzzp8.q: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the carriageway where vehicles are not allowed to stop
1lxzzp8.why: The Highway Code forbids both stopping (fermata) and parking (sosta) on pedestrian crossings, so pedestrians are not obstructed or hidden from view.

1j4lh0o.q: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the carriageway where vehicles must give way to pedestrians crossing on the marked stripes
1j4lh0o.why: A pedestrian crossing is part of the carriageway, and drivers must stop and give way to pedestrians crossing on it or about to step onto it.

2nrnxu.q: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the carriageway intended for pedestrians to cross
2nrnxu.why: A pedestrian crossing is the part of the carriageway, marked with white stripes, intended for pedestrians crossing from one side of the road to the other.

1k1m33o.q: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the carriageway where vehicles are not allowed to park
1k1m33o.why: Parking (sosta), and even briefly stopping (fermata), is forbidden on pedestrian crossings.

6jabxk.q: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the road separated from the carriageway by a yellow line
6jabxk.why: A pedestrian crossing is part of the carriageway and is marked by parallel white stripes; it is not separated from the carriageway by a yellow line.

15fqoit.q: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the carriageway that vehicles are forbidden to drive over
15fqoit.why: Vehicles may drive over a pedestrian crossing but must give way to pedestrians; only stopping and parking on it are forbidden.

1mj7kwh.q: A pedestrian crossing is not part of the carriageway
1mj7kwh.why: A pedestrian crossing is an integral part of the carriageway, just like lanes and cycle crossings.

dz9yfd.q: A pedestrian crossing is located outside the carriageway and is intended for pedestrian traffic
dz9yfd.why: A pedestrian crossing lies on the carriageway, not outside it: it is where pedestrians cross the part of the road used by vehicles.

1wntdat.q: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the carriageway where vehicles may stop briefly but not park
1wntdat.why: Both parking (sosta) and stopping (fermata) are forbidden on pedestrian crossings.

z58tt9.q: Main extra-urban roads (strade extraurbane principali) have separate carriageways
z58tt9.why: Primary extra-urban roads (strade extraurbane principali) have independent carriageways or ones separated by an uncrossable central reservation, with at least two lanes per direction.

zbn0f6.q: Main extra-urban roads have dedicated parking/rest areas
zbn0f6.why: The Highway Code requires primary extra-urban roads to have dedicated service and rest areas, reached via deceleration and acceleration lanes.

1nydbcy.q: A main extra-urban road has no at-grade junctions crossing it
1nydbcy.why: Primary extra-urban roads have no at-grade junctions: crossings with other roads are grade-separated (a livelli sfalsati).

1moq7ay.q: Main extra-urban roads are marked by start and end road signs
1moq7ay.why: The start and end of a primary extra-urban road are marked by specific signs, because special rules apply there, such as bans on certain vehicles.

8wec19.q: Only certain categories of motor vehicles may use main extra-urban roads
8wec19.why: A primary extra-urban road is reserved for certain categories of motor vehicles; mopeds, light quadricycles, agricultural machines, bicycles and pedestrians, for example, are excluded.

i4mr5f.q: On main extra-urban roads you may find grade-separated junctions (interchanges)
i4mr5f.why: Having no at-grade junctions, primary extra-urban roads connect to other roads through grade-separated junctions with ramps, overpasses and underpasses.

1d99okr.q: Main extra-urban roads have acceleration lanes for entering
1d99okr.why: Entries to primary extra-urban roads have acceleration lanes (corsie di accelerazione) for joining, and deceleration lanes for leaving.

u8z9b1.q: On main extra-urban roads you may drive at a maximum speed of 130 km/h
u8z9b1.why: The speed limit on primary extra-urban roads is 110 km/h; 130 km/h applies to motorways (autostrade).

1m3yzl9.q: Main extra-urban roads are identified by green signs
1m3yzl9.why: Direction signs on primary extra-urban roads have a blue background; green backgrounds identify motorways.

sxiccj.q: Main extra-urban roads may have a single carriageway
sxiccj.why: Primary extra-urban roads must have independent carriageways or ones separated by an uncrossable central reservation; a single-carriageway road cannot be one.

4xs25o.q: On main extra-urban roads you may drive at the same maximum speed as on motorways
4xs25o.why: The limit on primary extra-urban roads is 110 km/h, lower than the 130 km/h allowed on motorways.

734jle.q: Light quadricycles may use main extra-urban roads
734jle.why: Light quadricycles (quadricicli leggeri) are treated like mopeds and, like them, are banned from primary extra-urban roads.

sefmfc.q: Main extra-urban roads have only one lane in each direction
sefmfc.why: Primary extra-urban roads have at least two lanes per direction, plus a paved hard shoulder (banchina) on the right.

1u48dax.q: Mopeds may use main extra-urban roads
1u48dax.why: Mopeds (ciclomotori) are banned from primary extra-urban roads, as are light quadricycles, bicycles and pedestrians.

1nr351a.q: On main extra-urban roads there are no bends or humps
1nr351a.why: Primary extra-urban roads can have bends and humps like any road; what defines them is the absence of at-grade junctions, not of bends.

as3qhs.q: Main extra-urban roads must be equipped with variable message signs
as3qhs.why: The definition of a primary extra-urban road does not require variable message signs; the required features are separate carriageways, two or more lanes per direction, a right shoulder and no at-grade junctions.

u8t5yt.q: A traffic island (isola di traffico) helps channel vehicles toward different directions
u8t5yt.why: A traffic island (isola di traffico) is a non-drivable part of the road used to channel traffic flows toward different directions.

pipzm9.q: A traffic island is bordered by solid white lines
pipzm9.why: A flush traffic island is outlined by solid white lines and filled with white diagonal stripes (zebrature), which must not be driven over.

bkqpiv.q: A traffic island can be flush with the road surface or raised
bkqpiv.why: A traffic island can be flush (a raso), simply painted on the road with stripes, or raised (in rilievo) with a kerb.

1q1qrtb.q: A traffic island is highlighted with white zebra hatching
1q1qrtb.why: A traffic island is highlighted by white diagonal stripes (zebrature): a flush one consists of them, a raised one is preceded by them.

tc2ack.q: A traffic island is a part of the road where motorcycles are not allowed to drive
tc2ack.why: No vehicle may drive over a traffic island, so motorcycles are not allowed on it either.

1uipcyr.q: A flush (at-grade) traffic island is made up of white zebra hatching
1uipcyr.why: A flush traffic island is not raised: it consists of white diagonal stripes painted on the road and outlined by solid lines.

1pef227.q: A raised traffic island is preceded by white zebra hatching
1pef227.why: A raised traffic island is preceded by white diagonal stripes, which warn of the obstacle and guide vehicles around it.

11tvrpw.q: A traffic island is a part of the road where vehicles are not allowed to drive
11tvrpw.why: By definition a traffic island is a non-drivable part of the road: no vehicle may drive on it.

a7xwm.q: A traffic island serves to separate the carriageway from the hard shoulder
a7xwm.why: The carriageway is separated from the hard shoulder (banchina) by the edge line; a traffic island instead channels vehicles toward different directions.

iwg0xm.q: A traffic island is for pedestrians to walk on
iwg0xm.why: A traffic island channels vehicle traffic; pedestrians use pavements (marciapiedi), pedestrian crossings and safety refuges (salvagente).

13aur1e.q: A traffic island is a lay-by for vehicles to park
13aur1e.why: You may neither drive nor park on a traffic island: it only serves to channel traffic flows.

r7vxcq.q: A traffic island may be driven on only by taxis and city buses
r7vxcq.why: No vehicle may drive over a traffic island, taxis and buses included; it must not be confused with a reserved lane (corsia riservata).

h3r1si.q: A traffic island is the part of the city with the most traffic
h3r1si.why: A traffic island is not an area of the city but a road feature, flush or raised, that channels vehicles toward different directions.

nxs9qu.q: A traffic island generally corresponds to the historic centre of the city
nxs9qu.why: A traffic island has nothing to do with the historic centre: it is a non-drivable part of the road that channels traffic flows.

1u9t1tb.q: A traffic island is a lay-by for making U-turns
1u9t1tb.why: A traffic island cannot be driven on or used for a U-turn; it serves to channel vehicles toward different directions.

10dq253.q: A traffic island is located outside the road
10dq253.why: A traffic island is part of the road, usually located on the carriageway near junctions, to channel vehicle flows.

12mp0vq.q: A traffic island is for vehicles to stop on
12mp0vq.why: Driving onto a traffic island is forbidden, so stopping on it is too; its purpose is to channel traffic flows.

1l0mfn2.q: A traffic island makes it easier for passengers to get on and off trams, trolleybuses and buses
1l0mfn2.why: Passengers board and leave trams and buses at a safety island (salvagente); a traffic island instead channels vehicles.

1onz2du.q: A traffic island is an area intended for parking vehicles
1onz2du.why: A traffic island is not a car park: vehicles may not drive on or occupy it, and it only serves to channel traffic.

whbsvs.q: A traffic island is an urban pedestrian area
whbsvs.why: A pedestrian zone (area pedonale) is an area closed to vehicles and reserved for pedestrians; a traffic island is a road feature that channels vehicles.

heely7.q: A traffic island is a part of the road where mopeds are allowed to drive
heely7.why: No vehicle may drive on a traffic island, mopeds (ciclomotori) included.

1wvc7sj.q: A grade-separated junction (intersezione a livelli sfalsati) includes roads at different heights
1wvc7sj.why: In a grade-separated junction (intersezione a livelli sfalsati) the roads cross at different heights, for example one passing over the other on a flyover.

9hig9j.q: A grade-separated junction makes traffic flow more easily because it avoids vehicles crossing each other's paths directly
9hig9j.why: Because the roads are at different levels, traffic flows never cut across each other directly, and vehicles move between roads via ramps.

36swrt.q: A grade-separated junction includes ramps, overpasses or underpasses
36swrt.why: A grade-separated junction consists of overpasses or underpasses plus ramps connecting the roads at different heights.

qzr31q.q: A grade-separated junction is equipped with structures (ramps, overpasses, underpasses) connecting roads at different levels
qzr31q.why: Roads at different levels are linked by structures such as ramps, overpasses and underpasses, allowing vehicles to move between them without direct crossings.

1cf8b7m.q: A grade-separated junction is an at-grade crossing between a road and a railway line
1cf8b7m.why: An at-grade crossing between a road and a railway is a level crossing (passaggio a livello); a grade-separated junction links roads at different heights.

2h231e.q: At a grade-separated junction the general maximum speed limits do not apply
2h231e.why: The general speed limits, and any posted limits such as those on ramps, apply in grade-separated junctions too.

1kux9wg.q: A grade-separated junction is normally controlled by traffic lights
1kux9wg.why: Grade-separated junctions do not need traffic lights, because traffic flows never cross each other directly.

112585x.q: At an at-grade junction (intersezione a raso), two or more roads cross at the same level
112585x.why: In an at-grade junction (intersezione a raso) all roads meet at the same level, so traffic flows cross each other directly.

138zmir.q: An at-grade junction may be controlled by traffic lights
138zmir.why: Since vehicle flows cross directly, an at-grade junction can be controlled by traffic lights, priority signs or a traffic officer.

ml3wwy.q: An at-grade junction is an intersection of two or more roads at the same level
ml3wwy.why: An at-grade junction is the area shared by two or more roads that meet at the same level.

11dnmp2.q: An at-grade junction requires you to watch out for vehicles coming from the crossing roads
11dnmp2.why: At an at-grade junction vehicles from the different roads meet at the same level, so you must slow down and follow the right-of-way rules.

15t4jzq.q: An at-grade junction is a crossing between a state road and tram tracks
15t4jzq.why: An at-grade junction is where two or more roads cross at the same level; where a road crosses rails it is a level crossing or tram crossing.

uehi8j.q: An at-grade junction is a level crossing equipped with full or half barriers
uehi8j.why: A level crossing with full or half barriers is where a road meets a railway; an at-grade junction is instead where two or more roads meet at the same level.

czspuz.q: An at-grade junction is a grade-separated junction
czspuz.why: An at-grade junction is the opposite of a grade-separated one: the roads meet at the same height, not on different levels.

1daf2n1.q: An at-grade junction is a set of overpasses, underpasses and ramps
1daf2n1.why: Overpasses, underpasses and ramps belong to grade-separated junctions; in an at-grade junction the roads cross at the same level.

10qshef.q: An at-grade junction is a crossing between a state road and a private driveway (passo carrabile)
10qshef.why: A driveway entrance (passo carrabile) gives access to private property and is not a road; an at-grade junction is where two or more roads cross at the same level.

qv7fym.q: A limited traffic zone (ZTL) is an area where vehicle traffic may be restricted only at certain times
qv7fym.why: A limited traffic zone (zona a traffico limitato, ZTL) can restrict access only during certain hours, as shown on the supplementary panel under the entry sign.

ok88hs.q: A limited traffic zone (ZTL) is an area where traffic may be restricted only for particular categories of vehicles
ok88hs.why: In a ZTL, access can be restricted by time or by vehicle category, for example banning heavy goods vehicles while allowing others.

1s3umqh.q: In a limited traffic zone (ZTL) only authorised vehicles may circulate
1s3umqh.why: While the ZTL is active, only authorised vehicles, such as residents, public services or permit holders, may enter and drive in it.

1gdjx0y.q: A limited traffic zone (ZTL) is an area where traffic may be restricted to particular categories of users only
1gdjx0y.why: A ZTL can reserve access to particular categories of users, such as residents, disabled people, taxis or authorised delivery operators.

fzna3i.q: A limited traffic zone (ZTL) is marked by specific start and end road signs
fzna3i.why: The start and end of a ZTL are marked by specific road signs, often with electronic access gates that record entering vehicles.

1qpncdr.q: No more than a certain number of vehicles may enter a limited traffic zone (ZTL)
1qpncdr.why: A ZTL does not cap the number of vehicles; it restricts access by time of day, vehicle category or user category.

1u4vill.q: A limited traffic zone (ZTL) is an area where only mopeds and bicycles are allowed to pass
1u4vill.why: A ZTL is not reserved for mopeds and bicycles; any authorised vehicle may drive there, according to the set hours and categories.

qgy5eq.q: A limited traffic zone (ZTL) is an area always closed to motor vehicles
qgy5eq.why: A ZTL is not always closed to motor vehicles; authorised vehicles may enter, and restrictions may apply only at certain times.

1f9rbm2.q: A limited traffic zone (ZTL) is an area closed to pedestrians at night
1f9rbm2.why: A ZTL restricts vehicles, not pedestrians, who may always walk there at any hour.

1q0198r.q: At a level crossing there may be barriers
1q0198r.why: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) can be protected by full barriers that close the whole carriageway when a train approaches.

199nrsh.q: At a level crossing there may be half-barriers
199nrsh.why: A level crossing can have half barriers (semibarriere), which close only the right half of the carriageway in each direction.

15un80m.q: At a level crossing there may be red lights
15un80m.why: A level crossing can have flashing red lights that warn a train is coming and require you to stop.

1ayl097.q: Distance marker panels are found near a level crossing
1ayl097.why: Before a level crossing there are countdown marker boards (pannelli distanziometrici) with three, two and one red diagonal bars, at about 150, 100 and 50 m.

87gmx0.q: At a level crossing there may be a St Andrew's cross
87gmx0.why: The St Andrew's cross (croce di S. Andrea) is placed right by the tracks: single for one track, double for two or more tracks.

1o79hio.q: At a level crossing there may be an audible warning device
1o79hio.why: A level crossing can have an audible warning device, such as a bell, signalling that the barriers are about to close or a train is approaching.

qrh22p.q: A level crossing is a railway or tramway overpass
qrh22p.why: A level crossing is where a road crosses railway or tram tracks at the same level, not an overpass (cavalcavia).

1kekrbm.q: At a level crossing there may be flashing yellow lights
1kekrbm.why: Level crossing warning lights are flashing red, not yellow; they signal an approaching train and require you to stop.

14ht201.q: A level crossing is characterised by the presence of a motorway crossing
14ht201.why: A level crossing is an at-grade crossing between a road and a railway or tram line, not a motorway crossing.

a6csqc.q: At a level crossing there may be acceleration lanes
a6csqc.why: Acceleration lanes (corsie di accelerazione) are used to join motorways and main roads; they are not part of a level crossing.

pl3nd9.q: A level crossing is a driveway entrance (passo carrabile)
pl3nd9.why: A passo carrabile is a driveway access from private property to the road; a level crossing is where a road crosses tracks at the same level.

17seyz.q: A level crossing is characterised by the presence of an underpass
17seyz.why: At a level crossing the road and tracks cross at the same level; an underpass (sottopassaggio) is a grade-separated crossing instead.

vbdn35.q: Zero-emission (electric) vehicles may pass through pedestrian areas, if expressly permitted
vbdn35.why: Zero-emission vehicles, such as electric ones, may enter a pedestrian area (area pedonale) only if a specific municipal order allows it.

1wql7ff.q: Pedestrians may move through pedestrian areas
1wql7ff.why: A pedestrian area is intended precisely for pedestrians, who may move freely across the whole surface.

1ujh39y.q: Bicycles may pass through pedestrian areas
1ujh39y.why: The Highway Code allows bicycles in pedestrian areas; cyclists must ride carefully without getting in pedestrians' way.

dl181y.q: Vehicles serving people with disabilities may pass through pedestrian areas
dl181y.why: Vehicles serving people with disabilities and displaying the special permit (contrassegno) may drive in pedestrian areas.

1r4lved.q: Police vehicles may pass through pedestrian areas with their siren and blue flashing light on
1r4lved.why: Police vehicles on an emergency call, with siren and blue flashing light on, may drive through pedestrian areas.

1uhw9fo.q: Fire brigade vehicles may pass through pedestrian areas with their blue flashing light and siren on
1uhw9fo.why: Fire brigade vehicles on an emergency call, with siren and blue flashing light on, may drive through pedestrian areas.

mzid8.q: All motorcycles may pass through pedestrian areas, provided they give way to pedestrians
mzid8.why: Motorcycles may not enter pedestrian areas; only bicycles, emergency vehicles, vehicles for disabled people and specifically authorised vehicles are allowed.

1c4c887.q: Road tractors may pass through pedestrian areas at a speed not exceeding 30 km/h
1c4c887.why: Road tractors may not enter pedestrian areas at any speed; access is reserved for pedestrians, bicycles and expressly authorised vehicles.

fldha6.q: Mopeds may pass through pedestrian areas only during the day
fldha6.why: Mopeds (ciclomotori) may not drive in pedestrian areas either by day or by night, unless specifically authorised.

1unkxom.q: All motor vehicles may pass through pedestrian areas, but with caution
1unkxom.why: Motor vehicles may not drive in pedestrian areas; only emergency vehicles, vehicles serving disabled people or expressly authorised ones are allowed.

hi7yx6.q: Motor quadricycles may pass through pedestrian areas, provided they do not exceed 50 km/h
hi7yx6.why: Motor quadricycles are not allowed in pedestrian areas regardless of speed; the area is reserved for pedestrians, with only specific exceptions.

qlp2lp.q: A road may be divided into carriageways
qlp2lp.why: A road can have one or more carriageways (carreggiate), for example separated by a central reservation, as on motorways.

zlpkfb.q: A road may include cycle paths
zlpkfb.why: The road includes the whole public area, so cycle paths, pavements and hard shoulders as well as the carriageway.

1hsddjs.why: A road can be one-way (senso unico), with all vehicles travelling in the same direction.

1oc0jxf.why: A road can be two-way (doppio senso), with vehicles travelling in both directions.

1plaoei.q: A road is open to the movement of pedestrians, animals and vehicles
1plaoei.why: The Highway Code defines a road as a public area intended for the movement of pedestrians, vehicles and animals.

1u3cnyp.q: A road does not include the verges (banchine)
1u3cnyp.why: The road does include the hard shoulders (banchine); they are part of the road, though outside the carriageway.

mjqovw.q: A road is reserved for motor vehicles and motorcycles only
mjqovw.why: A road is not reserved for cars and motorcycles; it is intended for pedestrians, all kinds of vehicles and animals.

rerolp.q: A road is normally reserved for vehicles and animals only
rerolp.why: A road is not reserved for vehicles and animals only; it is also open to pedestrians.

17u5b0j.q: A road does not include the pavements
17u5b0j.why: Pavements (marciapiedi) are part of the road, though not of the carriageway, and are reserved for pedestrians.

1o3pesc.q: A road is any paved area bounded at the sides by pedestrian crossings
1o3pesc.why: A road is a public area for pedestrians, vehicles and animals, regardless of its surface or of any pedestrian crossings.

pnw8q5.q: A motorway has no level (at-grade) intersections crossing it
pnw8q5.why: A motorway (autostrada) has no at-grade junctions; other roads cross it on different levels via overpasses or underpasses.

1nxsvqa.q: A motorway has special lanes for vehicles entering and exiting
1nxsvqa.why: A motorway has acceleration lanes for joining and deceleration lanes for leaving.

164udgt.q: A motorway has independent carriageways or carriageways separated by a central reservation
164udgt.why: A motorway has independent carriageways or ones divided by an uncrossable central reservation, each with at least two lanes per direction.

xsmzah.q: Motorcycles with an engine capacity of at least 150 cc may use the motorway
xsmzah.why: Motorcycles of at least 120 cm³ ridden by adults are allowed on motorways (the limit was 150 cm³ before the 2024 reform), so 150 cm³ bikes certainly are.

1m2sce8.q: Agricultural machines may not use the motorway
1m2sce8.why: Agricultural machines are too slow and are banned from motorways, together with mopeds, bicycles, pedestrians and small motorcycles.

1g4poeu.q: Not all types of vehicles may use the motorway
1g4poeu.why: Pedestrians, animals, bicycles, mopeds, agricultural machines, light quadricycles and small motorcycles are all banned from motorways.

rf687t.q: Vehicles exit motorways via deceleration lanes
rf687t.why: To leave a motorway you move into the deceleration lane (corsia di decelerazione) and slow down there without hindering through traffic.

1glnk0f.q: A motorway must be fenced along its sides
1glnk0f.why: By definition a motorway is fenced along its sides, to keep pedestrians and animals out.

cyvxdx.why: Not only cars use motorways; lorries, buses, motorhomes and motorcycles of sufficient engine size are allowed too.

1ddt18k.q: All types of motorcycles may use motorways
1ddt18k.why: Not all motorcycles are allowed; those under 120 cm³, or ridden by under-18s, may not use the motorway.

g23e2d.q: A motorway may include cycle paths
g23e2d.why: A motorway cannot include cycle paths, because bicycles are banned from motorways.

bp28oi.q: Mopeds and motorcycles up to 125 cc may use motorways
bp28oi.why: Mopeds (ciclomotori) are never allowed on motorways, and small-capacity motorcycles are excluded as well.

f89vg4.q: Only motor vehicles (autoveicoli) may use motorways
f89vg4.why: Motorcycles of sufficient engine size are also allowed on motorways, and they are not autoveicoli (four-wheeled motor vehicles).

1ki29gb.q: All motorcycles and mopeds may use motorways
1ki29gb.why: Mopeds are always banned from motorways, and so are motorcycles under 120 cm³.

1qbk16h.why: A carriageway can be one-way, like each of the separate carriageways of a motorway.

ovaczw.why: A carriageway can be two-way, with lanes for both directions, as on most secondary rural roads.

1lwqu8x.q: A carriageway may be divided into lanes
1lwqu8x.why: A carriageway is usually divided into lanes (corsie), marked by continuous or broken longitudinal lines.

1oynakl.q: A carriageway does not include cycle paths
1oynakl.why: Cycle paths (piste ciclabili) are part of the road but not of the carriageway, which is intended for vehicle traffic.

nn47ww.q: A carriageway does not include pavements
nn47ww.why: Pavements are outside the carriageway, raised or otherwise separated, and reserved for pedestrians.

1kro6kh.q: The carriageway is the part of the road normally intended for vehicle traffic
1kro6kh.why: The Highway Code defines the carriageway (carreggiata) as the part of the road intended for vehicles, made up of one or more lanes.

r43qj0.q: The carriageway is intended only for animal-drawn carts
r43qj0.why: The carriageway is for all vehicles, not only animal-drawn carts.

1j5890v.q: The carriageway is intended for emergency stops
1j5890v.why: The carriageway is for traffic; emergency stops are made in the emergency lane or in lay-bys (piazzole), which are outside the carriageway.

dkrak1.q: The carriageway is intended for parking lorries
dkrak1.why: The carriageway is for moving vehicles, not for parking lorries, which must use designated areas.

1di70q9.q: The carriageway is the track left by vehicle wheels on snow-covered roads
1di70q9.why: The carriageway is the part of the road meant for vehicles, not the tracks left by wheels in the snow.

pj2q78.why: Lay-bys (piazzole di sosta) are outside the carriageway, built at the roadside for emergency stops.

80p1ak.q: Traffic lanes are part of the carriageway
80p1ak.why: The carriageway is made up of one or more traffic lanes (corsie di marcia) for vehicles.

195t180.q: Cycle crossings are part of the carriageway
195t180.why: Cycle crossings (attraversamenti ciclabili) are marked on the carriageway so cyclists can cross it.

1n8xp8c.q: Pedestrian crossings are part of the carriageway
1n8xp8c.why: Pedestrian crossings (attraversamenti pedonali, zebra crossings) are marked on the carriageway, so they are part of it.

13obhz1.q: Overtaking lanes are part of the carriageway
13obhz1.why: Overtaking lanes (corsie di sorpasso) are lanes of the carriageway, used to pass slower vehicles.

1bjyoiz.q: Motorway emergency lanes are part of the carriageway
1bjyoiz.why: The motorway emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) runs beside the carriageway but is not part of it; it is for emergency stops.

1aqx9t.q: The verges (banchine) are part of the carriageway
1aqx9t.why: Hard shoulders (banchine) are parts of the road outside the carriageway, beyond the white edge line, and not meant for vehicle traffic.

12vlrtv.q: Pavements are part of the carriageway
12vlrtv.why: Pavements are outside the carriageway, raised or otherwise separated, and reserved for pedestrians.

1nrtmej.q: A lane may be intended for the normal movement of vehicles
1nrtmej.why: A traffic lane (corsia di marcia) is intended for the normal flow of vehicles.

1itsx2u.q: A lane is bounded by continuous or broken lines
1itsx2u.why: Lanes are marked by white longitudinal lines on the carriageway, either continuous or broken.

s7qfoo.q: A lane may be an acceleration lane
s7qfoo.why: An acceleration lane lets you build up speed to join motorways and main extra-urban roads.

tgxk5l.q: A lane may be a deceleration lane
tgxk5l.why: A deceleration lane lets you slow down to leave the carriageway without hindering through traffic.

14jretw.q: Lanes may be closed to certain types of vehicles
14jretw.why: With specific signs, a lane can be closed to certain vehicles, for example lorries banned from the overtaking lane.

1f1oiru.q: A lane may be reserved for certain categories of vehicles (taxis, buses, etc.)
1f1oiru.why: Some lanes are reserved for specific vehicles, such as buses and taxis, marked with yellow lines and signs.

mbr153.q: A lane may be intended for overtaking
mbr153.why: On carriageways with several lanes per direction, the left-hand lanes are for overtaking.

bd45nu.q: The road owner may require vehicles in a lane to travel at a mandatory minimum speed
bd45nu.why: The road owner can impose a compulsory minimum speed on a lane, shown by a round blue sign with the value in km/h.

1ywbk9g.q: A lane is a part of the carriageway that allows a single line of vehicles to travel
1ywbk9g.why: The Highway Code defines a lane as a longitudinal strip of the carriageway wide enough for a single line of vehicles.

1fo5qf.q: A lane may be intended for emergency stops in case of breakdown or illness
1fo5qf.why: The emergency lane (corsia di emergenza), beside motorway carriageways, is for stopping in case of breakdown or illness and for rescue vehicles.

1nd6s4e.q: A lane may be reserved for vehicles intending to turn (dedicated turning lane)
1nd6s4e.why: A specialised lane (corsia specializzata) is reserved for vehicles turning or making a specific manoeuvre near a junction.

w70xrt.q: A lane may be intended for vehicles slowing down as they exit the motorway
w70xrt.why: The deceleration lane is used to slow down when leaving the motorway without hindering traffic.

1hr9tpy.q: A lane is intended only for pedestrians
1hr9tpy.why: A lane is part of the carriageway intended for vehicles; pedestrians must use pavements, hard shoulders and pedestrian crossings.

zob7h1.q: A lane may carry two-way traffic
zob7h1.why: A lane carries a single line of vehicles, so it has only one direction; it is the carriageway that can be two-way.

11n6bfy.q: A lane is a track reserved for racing cars
11n6bfy.why: A lane is the part of the carriageway for a single line of vehicles in normal traffic, not a track for racing cars.

w6e0t5.q: Pedestrians may never cross a lane
w6e0t5.why: Pedestrians may cross lanes, for example on pedestrian crossings, which are part of the carriageway and therefore lie across the lanes.

1anvuyl.q: A lane is made up of two carriageways
1anvuyl.why: It is the other way round: the carriageway (carreggiata) is divided into one or more lanes (corsie). A lane is a longitudinal strip wide enough for a single file of vehicles.

1hm4nez.q: A lane (corsia) is a fast-flowing road
1hm4nez.why: A lane (corsia) is not a type of road but a longitudinal strip of the carriageway, wide enough for a single file of vehicles.

1i4cs7h.q: In built-up areas, two motorcycles may ride side by side in the same lane
1i4cs7h.why: A lane is wide enough for only one file of vehicles, in towns too: two motorcycles may not ride side by side in the same lane.

1rtuypd.q: Outside built-up areas, two mopeds may ride side by side in the same lane
1rtuypd.why: A lane carries only one file of vehicles: mopeds (ciclomotori) must ride in single file, never side by side in the same lane.

yuh6v8.q: The acceleration lane makes it easier for vehicles to enter the motorway or a primary extra-urban road
yuh6v8.why: The acceleration lane lets you reach a suitable speed before merging into the traffic of motorways and main extra-urban roads (strade extraurbane principali).

14sxmh1.q: The acceleration lane is used to enter the motorway correctly
14sxmh1.why: You use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and merge safely onto the motorway carriageway, giving way to vehicles already on it.

7jc03w.q: The acceleration lane is used to increase speed
7jc03w.why: The acceleration lane exists precisely to let you increase speed up to that of the traffic you are about to join.

hd3ukg.q: The acceleration lane is used to rejoin the motorway carriageway after leaving a service area
hd3ukg.why: Service areas are linked to the motorway by a deceleration lane on the way in and an acceleration lane on the way out, which you use to rejoin the carriageway.

1c37tov.q: The acceleration lane may be used for overtaking
1c37tov.why: The acceleration lane is only for merging onto the main carriageway; it may not be used for overtaking.

1a9nmhl.q: The acceleration lane is used to leave an emergency lay-by (piazzola di sosta)
1a9nmhl.why: Emergency lay-bys (piazzole di sosta) have no acceleration lanes; those are for joining motorways or main extra-urban roads, e.g. from junctions or service areas.

1w9yxsn.q: The acceleration lane is used to leave the motorway carriageway and enter a rest area
1w9yxsn.why: To leave the motorway and enter a service area you use the deceleration lane; the acceleration lane is for rejoining it.

19741jt.q: The deceleration lane makes it easier for vehicles to exit the motorway
19741jt.why: The deceleration lane lets you leave the carriageway and slow down without hindering through traffic, making it easier to exit the motorway.

t3r7yr.q: The deceleration lane is used to exit a primary extra-urban road correctly
t3r7yr.why: Main extra-urban roads also have deceleration lanes: you move into them and slow down there to exit correctly.

ee67oj.q: The deceleration lane is used to leave the motorway carriageway and enter the service area
ee67oj.why: To enter a service area you leave the motorway carriageway via the deceleration lane, where you reduce speed.

6akogd.q: The deceleration lane may be used for parking vehicles
6akogd.why: Parking is forbidden in the deceleration lane; it is only for slowing down and leaving the main carriageway.

zz911a.q: The deceleration lane is used to enter an emergency lay-by (piazzola di sosta)
zz911a.why: Emergency lay-bys are entered directly from the carriageway, without a deceleration lane; that lane is for leaving the motorway or entering service areas.

1ep6hod.q: The deceleration lane is used to enter the motorway
1ep6hod.why: You join the motorway using the acceleration lane; the deceleration lane is for leaving it.

ztw3tb.q: The hard shoulder (banchina) does not, as a rule, allow vehicles to travel on it
ztw3tb.why: The hard shoulder (banchina) lies outside the carriageway and is normally not meant for vehicle traffic, except in emergencies or where signs allow it.

gvokrw.q: The hard shoulder (banchina) is part of the road, located outside the carriageway
gvokrw.why: The hard shoulder (banchina) is part of the road but lies outside the carriageway (carreggiata), beyond the solid white edge line.

1va4dn6.q: The hard shoulder (banchina) is part of the road, located beyond the solid white edge line of the carriageway
1va4dn6.why: The solid white edge line marks the end of the carriageway; beyond it lies the hard shoulder (banchina), which is still part of the road.

polhu9.q: The hard shoulder (banchina) is reserved for slow vehicles on uphill roads
polhu9.why: The hard shoulder is not reserved for slow vehicles; on uphill stretches they have a climbing lane (corsia di arrampicata), which is part of the carriageway.

9b9uf0.q: Vehicles may park on the hard shoulder (banchina) for up to 5 hours
9b9uf0.why: The Code sets no 5-hour limit for the hard shoulder; it is not meant for traffic, and on motorways and main extra-urban roads you may stop there only in an emergency.

7p9lgd.q: The hard shoulder (banchina) divides the carriageway into two lanes
7p9lgd.why: Lanes are separated by longitudinal lines painted on the carriageway; the hard shoulder (banchina) lies outside the carriageway.

tval8t.q: The hard shoulder (banchina) is part of the carriageway, intended for parking vehicles
tval8t.why: The hard shoulder is not part of the carriageway: it lies outside it, beyond the edge line, and is not intended for parking.

10owuqp.q: The pavement (marciapiede) is a part of the road, raised or otherwise separated, reserved for pedestrians
10owuqp.why: The pavement (marciapiede) is the part of the road outside the carriageway, raised or otherwise separated and protected, reserved for pedestrians.

1at1tc.q: The pavement (marciapiede) is a part of the road normally reserved for pedestrians
1at1tc.why: The pavement is meant for pedestrians; vehicles may only cross it to reach a vehicle access (passo carrabile) or park on it where specifically marked.

1y368ah.q: Vehicles may park on the pavement (marciapiede) only where there are specific parking bay markings
1y368ah.why: Parking on the pavement is forbidden unless otherwise indicated: it is allowed only where specific parking bays are marked.

16qa87x.q: The pavement (marciapiede) is a part of the road, outside the carriageway, intended for pedestrian traffic
16qa87x.why: The pavement lies outside the carriageway and is reserved for pedestrian traffic.

zne915.q: The pavement (marciapiede) is part of the carriageway
zne915.why: The pavement is not part of the carriageway (carreggiata); it is a separate, raised or delimited part of the road reserved for pedestrians.

2rdc6w.q: The pavement (marciapiede) is a part of the road also reserved for bicycles
2rdc6w.why: The pavement is reserved for pedestrians; bicycles may use it only where it is signed as a shared cycle-pedestrian path, otherwise they must be walked.

1eig1wz.q: The pavement (marciapiede) is reserved for pedestrians and parked vehicles if it is not raised
1eig1wz.why: The pavement is reserved for pedestrians whether raised or delimited in another way; vehicles may not park on it unless bays are marked.

12hx9mr.q: The pavement (marciapiede) is a part of the road where mopeds are normally allowed to park
12hx9mr.why: Parking on the pavement is forbidden for all vehicles, mopeds included, except in specifically marked areas.

cjzrr7.q: The pedestrian refuge island (salvagente), located at pedestrian crossings, also serves to shelter pedestrians or let them wait while crossing the road
cjzrr7.why: The pedestrian refuge (salvagente) is a raised or delimited area that gives pedestrians a safe place to stop halfway across the road at crossings.

1vkkpxy.q: The pedestrian refuge island (salvagente) makes it easier for passengers to get on and off trams, trolleybuses or buses
1vkkpxy.why: The pedestrian refuge (salvagente) is for pedestrians and is used in particular for boarding and alighting from trams, trolleybuses and buses.

1x83f7x.q: The pedestrian refuge island (salvagente) may be marked by illuminated posts with a steady yellow light
1x83f7x.why: To make it visible, especially at night, the pedestrian refuge may be marked by bollards with a fixed yellow light.

1ufzylh.q: The pedestrian refuge island (salvagente) serves to separate the directions of travel on a two-way road
1ufzylh.why: The refuge is an area for pedestrians; directions of traffic are separated by a central reservation (spartitraffico) or the centre line.

4diaxm.q: The pedestrian refuge island (salvagente) serves to channel vehicles in various directions
4diaxm.why: Channelling vehicles in different directions is the job of the traffic island (isola di traffico); the refuge (salvagente) is for pedestrians.

1hpheys.q: The salvagente is a person in charge of first aid
1hpheys.why: In the Highway Code a salvagente is not a person but a raised or delimited part of the road where pedestrians can wait safely.

1ov9ucu.q: The salvagente is a combined cycle and pedestrian route
1ov9ucu.why: The refuge is a small waiting area for pedestrians, not a route; a cycle-pedestrian route (itinerario ciclopedonale) is a road meant for pedestrians and cyclists.

va1whv.q: The vehicle access point (passo carrabile) lets vehicles enter private properties alongside the road (garages, courtyards, etc.)
va1whv.why: A vehicle access (passo carrabile) lets vehicles enter and leave private properties beside the road, such as garages and courtyards.

cneohv.q: The vehicle access point (passo carrabile) allows vehicles travelling on a public road to enter an adjacent area used for parking
cneohv.why: Through a vehicle access (passo carrabile) vehicles leave the public road to reach side areas, including ones used for parking.

14s1qxg.q: The vehicle access point (passo carrabile) must have a specific sign showing the issuing authority and the authorisation number
14s1qxg.why: A vehicle access must display the official sign showing the road authority that issued it and the authorisation number and year.

1wcvc32.q: The vehicle access point (passo carrabile) is an area allowing vehicles to access properties alongside the road
1wcvc32.why: A vehicle access (passo carrabile) is exactly the area that lets vehicles reach properties located beside the road.

i2wcq9.q: Stopping briefly (fermata) is allowed at a vehicle access point (passo carrabile)
i2wcq9.why: Only parking is banned in front of a vehicle access; stopping, a brief halt with the driver present (fermata), is allowed.

5qgble.q: The vehicle access point (passo carrabile) is a park-and-ride car park
5qgble.why: A vehicle access serves properties beside the road; a park-and-ride (parcheggio scambiatore) is a car park linked to public transport.

19mq52d.q: The passo carrabile is a road reserved for animal-drawn carts
19mq52d.why: A vehicle access (passo carrabile) is not a road; it is the entrance that lets any vehicle reach properties beside the road.

3e48br.q: The passo carrabile is a road reserved for lorries
3e48br.why: A vehicle access is not a road reserved for lorries but the point where vehicles enter properties beside the road.

5hpjeq.q: The passo carrabile is a circular pedestrian refuge island
5hpjeq.why: A vehicle access is for vehicles entering side properties; the pedestrian refuge (salvagente) is the area where pedestrians wait.

1syqmqp.q: The passo carrabile is a sign requiring traffic to go round a square
1syqmqp.why: A vehicle access is not a mandatory sign but an entrance to side properties; roundabout circulation is imposed by a different sign.

ppv8xx.q: Parking (sosta) is allowed at a vehicle access point (passo carrabile)
ppv8xx.why: Parking in front of a vehicle access is forbidden because it would block the entrance; only a brief stop (fermata) is allowed.

1o7g4xq.q: Two-wheeled vehicles with an internal combustion engine of up to 50 cm³ and a maximum speed of 45 km/h are mopeds (ciclomotori)
1o7g4xq.why: Mopeds (ciclomotori) are two- or three-wheeled vehicles with a combustion engine up to 50 cm3 (or electric up to 4 kW) and a top design speed not above 45 km/h.

1ix83so.q: Mopeds (ciclomotori) may have two or three wheels
1ix83so.why: The Code defines mopeds as motor vehicles with two or three wheels within the limits of 50 cm3 (or 4 kW) and 45 km/h.

bno3pl.q: Not all two-wheeled motor vehicles are classified as mopeds (ciclomotori)
bno3pl.why: A two-wheeler is a moped only if it does not exceed 50 cm3 (or 4 kW) and 45 km/h; beyond these limits it is a motorcycle (motociclo).

1xa57nj.q: Two-wheeled mopeds (ciclomotori) cannot have an internal combustion engine larger than 50 cm³
1xa57nj.why: The limit for mopeds with a combustion engine is 50 cm3; above that the vehicle is classed as a motorcycle.

1567eu2.q: Mopeds (ciclomotori) must undergo a roadworthiness test (revisione) four years after first registration, and every two years after that
1567eu2.why: Mopeds must undergo their first roadworthiness test (revisione) four years after first registration, and every two years after that.

mbfbsu.q: Mopeds (ciclomotori) have no more than two wheels
mbfbsu.why: Mopeds can also have three wheels, as long as they stay within 50 cm3 (or 4 kW) and 45 km/h.

yjrksn.q: Pedal-assisted bicycles fitted with an auxiliary electric motor of up to 0.25 kW maximum power are classified as mopeds (ciclomotori)
yjrksn.why: Pedal-assisted bicycles with a motor up to 0.25 kW that cuts out at 25 km/h or when you stop pedalling are bicycles (velocipedi), not mopeds.

xky1vq.q: All two-wheeled vehicles with an engine larger than 50 cm³ are classified as mopeds (ciclomotori)
xky1vq.why: Two-wheelers above 50 cm3 are motorcycles (motocicli); mopeds have at most 50 cm3 and 45 km/h.

1c5use0.q: To be classified as such, mopeds (ciclomotori) must have a manual gearbox
1c5use0.why: The type of gearbox is irrelevant: a moped is defined by engine size (up to 50 cm3) or power (up to 4 kW) and a top speed of 45 km/h.

1nzq7ml.q: Mopeds (ciclomotori) may travel at 60 km/h outside urban areas
1nzq7ml.why: Mopeds may not exceed 45 km/h, their maximum design speed, both inside and outside built-up areas.

qyv7gm.q: Mopeds (ciclomotori) are not subject to periodic roadworthiness tests (revisione)
qyv7gm.why: Mopeds are subject to periodic testing (revisione): first after four years from registration, then every two years.

1tqt63f.q: Motor tricycles (tricicli a motore) are motor vehicles with three symmetrically arranged wheels
1tqt63f.why: Motor tricycles (tricicli a motore) are vehicles with three symmetrically arranged wheels, above 50 cm3 or capable of more than 45 km/h.

bmkyuq.q: Motor tricycles (tricicli a motore) are vehicles with an engine larger than 50 cm³
bmkyuq.why: Above 50 cm3, a vehicle with three symmetrical wheels is no longer a moped but a motor tricycle.

4bnzc5.q: Motor tricycles (tricicli a motore) are motor vehicles with a design maximum speed above 45 km/h
4bnzc5.why: Motor tricycles can exceed 45 km/h by design, the limit above which a three-wheeler is no longer a moped.

2gybgs.q: Motor tricycles (tricicli a motore) must undergo a roadworthiness test (revisione) four years after first registration, and every two years after that
2gybgs.why: Like mopeds, motor tricycles have their first test four years after first registration and then every two years.

1m6xrkg.q: Motor tricycles (tricicli a motore) are motor vehicles that can be driven without a licence
1m6xrkg.why: A driving licence is required for a motor tricycle (A1, A or B depending on power and the driver's age).

3ot9w7.q: Motor tricycles (tricicli a motore) consist of a motorcycle and a sidecar
3ot9w7.why: A motorcycle with a sidecar is still a motorcycle because its wheels are not symmetrical; motor tricycles have three symmetrical wheels.

irc4yb.q: Motor tricycles (tricicli a motore) are vehicles with an engine smaller than 50 cm³ and a design maximum speed of up to 45 km/h
irc4yb.why: Up to 50 cm3 and 45 km/h a three-wheeler is a moped; motor tricycles exceed these limits.

wthj38.q: Motor tricycles (tricicli a motore) are not subject to periodic roadworthiness tests (revisione)
wthj38.why: Motor tricycles are subject to periodic testing: four years after first registration, then every two years.

ub2qz9.q: Petrol-powered light quadricycles (quadricicli leggeri) have an engine capacity of 50 cm³ or less
ub2qz9.why: Petrol light quadricycles (quadricicli leggeri) have engines of no more than 50 cm3 and a top speed of 45 km/h, like mopeds.

ybsada.why: Quadricycles are four-wheeled motor vehicles, split into light and non-light according to mass, engine size or power, and speed.

1lwuuj9.q: For traffic purposes, light quadricycles (quadricicli leggeri) are treated as mopeds (ciclomotori)
1lwuuj9.why: For traffic purposes light quadricycles are treated as mopeds: they follow moped rules and are driven with an AM licence.

7tjxes.q: The power of non-light quadricycles is always 15 kW or less
7tjxes.why: The Code sets a maximum power of 15 kW for non-light quadricycles.

7jnavx.q: Quadricycles (quadricicli) are subject to periodic roadworthiness tests (revisione)
7jnavx.why: All quadricycles, light or not, must undergo periodic roadworthiness tests (revisione).

r9u44.q: Quadricycles other than light ones may be driven without a licence
r9u44.why: Non-light quadricycles require a B1 licence, available from age 16, or a higher licence such as B.

1d1qlb3.q: For traffic purposes, non-light quadricycles are treated the same as mopeds (ciclomotori)
1d1qlb3.why: Only light quadricycles are treated as mopeds; non-light ones are motor vehicles (motoveicoli) requiring a B1 licence.

99bsc4.q: It is permitted to replace the exhaust system of a light quadricycle to increase its maximum speed, as long as the engine capacity is not increased
99bsc4.why: Modifying a light quadricycle, including its exhaust, to raise its speed above 45 km/h is forbidden, as it alters the approved specifications.

u2drtx.q: Non-light quadricycles may already be driven from the age of fourteen
u2drtx.why: At 14, with an AM licence, you may drive only light quadricycles; non-light ones require a B1 licence, from age 16.

1wnvq9n.q: Non-light quadricycles with handlebars and an open body may be ridden without a helmet
1wnvq9n.why: A helmet is compulsory on handlebar quadricycles with open bodywork; only vehicles with closed bodywork and seat belts are exempt.

bjjof1.q: It is permitted to increase the engine capacity of a light quadricycle as long as its speed is not increased
bjjof1.why: You may not increase the engine size of a light quadricycle: its approved specifications, such as 50 cm3 and 45 km/h, must not be altered.

1ajrf3u.q: It is permitted to replace the engine of a light quadricycle to raise its maximum speed above 45 km/h
1ajrf3u.why: Replacing a light quadricycle's engine to exceed 45 km/h is forbidden; the vehicle would no longer match its type approval.

qefrpy.q: Quadricycles (quadricicli) are not subject to periodic roadworthiness tests (revisione)
qefrpy.why: Quadricycles, light or not, are subject to periodic roadworthiness tests like other motor vehicles.

1biatuk.q: Agricultural machines (macchine agricole) may travel on the road to move from place to place if they are registered
1biatuk.why: Registered agricultural machines may travel on public roads to move from one place to another, e.g. from the farm to the field.

16vywyk.q: Agricultural machines (macchine agricole) may be wheeled or tracked
16vywyk.why: The Code classifies agricultural machines as wheeled or tracked vehicles designed for farm work.

1m2l41q.q: Wheeled or tracked agricultural machines may travel on the road to transport agricultural products on behalf of farming and forestry businesses
1m2l41q.why: Agricultural machines may also use public roads to carry farm produce and agricultural supplies on behalf of farming and forestry businesses.

5sz0hi.q: Agricultural machines (macchine agricole) may be self-propelled or towed
5sz0hi.why: Agricultural machines are either self-propelled (semoventi), like tractors, or towed (trainate), like farm trailers.

38sxof.q: Agricultural operating machines may be fitted with special equipment for carrying out farming operations
38sxof.why: Agricultural working machines (macchine agricole operatrici) carry special equipment to perform farm operations, such as combine harvesters and sprayers.

1u4fzyi.q: Operating machines (macchine operatrici) may be self-propelled or towed
1u4fzyi.why: The Code divides working machines (macchine operatrici), used for construction, roadworks or snow clearing, into self-propelled and towed.

17c88sf.q: Operating machines (macchine operatrici) can be snowploughs
17c88sf.why: Operating machines (macchine operatrici) are self-propelled or towed vehicles used for road or site work, such as snowploughs, road-maintenance and construction vehicles.

s8obxs.q: Operating machines may travel at a speed above 50 km/h
s8obxs.why: Operating machines on tyres may not exceed 40 km/h, and tracked ones are limited to 15 km/h, so going above 50 km/h is never allowed.

1cio9oe.q: Tracked operating machines may travel at a speed above 45 km/h
1cio9oe.why: Tracked operating machines (a cingoli) have a speed limit of 15 km/h, far below 45 km/h.

13cvsto.q: Self-propelled operating machines may carry up to four passengers
13cvsto.why: Self-propelled operating machines are not meant to carry passengers: only the driver and any working crew may be on board, in the seats listed in the registration document.

1gptdzk.q: To drive operating machines you must hold a category A driving licence
1gptdzk.why: Normal operating machines require a category B licence, and oversized (eccezionali) ones a category C licence; a category A licence does not cover them.

mh93ae.q: Agricultural machines (macchine agricole) may carry up to four passengers
mh93ae.why: Self-propelled agricultural machines may have at most three seats, including the driver's, if listed in the registration document.

28fdxe.q: Carrying standing passengers is allowed on agricultural machines and their trailers
28fdxe.why: On agricultural machines and their trailers people may only travel in the approved seats; standing is forbidden.

170x8es.q: With a category A licence you can drive all agricultural machines
170x8es.why: A category A licence covers only small agricultural machines within set size and mass limits; others need a B licence, and oversized (eccezionali) ones a C licence.

1ou3dor.q: With a category B licence you can drive oversize (eccezionali) operating machines
1ou3dor.why: A category B licence only covers normal operating machines; oversized ones (macchine operatrici eccezionali) require a category C licence.

yv2mf4.q: Caravans (roulottes) are trailers equipped to be used as living accommodation
yv2mf4.why: A caravan (roulotte) is a trailer with a body permanently fitted out to be used as living accommodation, but only while parked.

1aahd6j.q: Caravans (roulottes) may be used as accommodation only when the vehicle is stationary
1aahd6j.why: A caravan can be used as accommodation only when stationary; nobody may ride inside it while it is being towed.

18s4kk0.q: Caravans (roulottes) are fitted with a number plate
18s4kk0.why: Like other trailers, a caravan must carry its own number plate (targa), separate from the towing vehicle's.

p2gdsp.q: It is allowed to stay inside a caravan (roulotte) while it is being driven
p2gdsp.why: A caravan may be used as accommodation only when parked; carrying people inside it while on the move is forbidden.

kuodkh.q: Caravans (roulottes) are trailers intended for agricultural work
kuodkh.why: A caravan is a trailer fitted out as living accommodation when parked; trailers for farm work are towed agricultural machines.

1o9eohg.q: Caravans (roulottes) are trailers intended exclusively for carrying tourist and sports equipment
1o9eohg.why: A caravan is a trailer fitted out as living accommodation when parked, not a trailer used only to carry tourist or sports equipment.

157st5h.q: Motor caravans (autocaravan, camper) are vehicles with special bodywork designed for transporting and accommodating people
157st5h.why: A motorhome (autocaravan) is a motor vehicle with a special body permanently fitted out to carry people and provide them with accommodation.

1m0dbvt.q: Motor caravans (camper) are vehicles with special bodywork designed for transporting and accommodating at most the number of people stated in the registration document
1m0dbvt.why: A motorhome (autocaravan) may carry and accommodate at most the number of people stated in its registration document (carta di circolazione).

9s4lam.q: Motor caravans (camper) are vehicles permanently equipped for transporting and accommodating people
9s4lam.why: A motorhome's interior fittings are fixed and permanent, because the vehicle is designed both to transport people and to house them.

1wzd5q6.q: Motor caravans are subject to periodic roadworthiness tests (revisione)
1wzd5q6.why: Like cars, motorhomes must undergo periodic inspection (revisione): first after 4 years from registration, then every 2 years.

323hyr.why: A motorhome (autocaravan) is a motor vehicle with its own engine; the trailer equivalent used for accommodation is the caravan.

o21cqj.q: Motor caravans (camper) are vehicles intended for agricultural work
o21cqj.why: A motorhome is meant to transport and accommodate people; vehicles for farm work are agricultural machines (macchine agricole).

1hidwpx.q: Motor caravans (camper) are vehicles intended for building and maintaining roadworks
1hidwpx.why: A motorhome is for transporting and housing people; vehicles for building and maintaining roads are operating machines (macchine operatrici).

bon61k.q: On motor caravans (camper) you may travel standing, but only for short stretches
bon61k.why: While a motorhome is moving, everyone must sit in the seats listed in the registration document, wearing seat belts where fitted, even for short distances.

hkm7si.q: Motor caravans are subject to a roadworthiness test (revisione) every five years
hkm7si.why: Motorhomes follow the same schedule as cars: first inspection 4 years after registration, then every 2 years.

k5hbjf.q: When on the road, lorries with a maximum laden mass above 3.5 tonnes must be marked at the rear with the reflective panels shown
k5hbjf.why: Panels with alternating diagonal yellow and red stripes are fitted at the rear of lorries (autocarri) with a maximum mass over 3.5 t.

3k9pv3.q: When on the road, goods trailers and semi-trailers with a maximum laden mass above 3.5 tonnes must be marked at the rear with the reflective panels shown
3k9pv3.why: The yellow panel with a red border is fitted at the rear of goods trailers and semi-trailers with a maximum mass over 3.5 t.

kpiv9.q: When on the road, lorries and trailers with a maximum laden mass above 3.5 t must be marked with rear and side reflective strips
kpiv9.why: Lorries and trailers over 3.5 t must carry reflective strips outlining their shape: red or yellow at the rear, white or yellow on the sides.

hpmbz3.q: The panel shown indicates the transport of dangerous goods
hpmbz3.why: The orange panel marks dangerous goods: the top number is the hazard code (Kemler code) and the bottom number identifies the substance (UN number).

1sdv5xb.q: The panel shown indicates a load that sticks out beyond the vehicle (carico sporgente)
1sdv5xb.why: The square panel with diagonal red and white stripes must be fixed to the end of a load that sticks out beyond the vehicle (carico sporgente).

bipytx.q: Reflective strips fitted on the sides of some vehicles may be white or yellow
bipytx.why: Side reflective strips may be white or yellow, while rear strips are red or yellow.

qijoqk.q: Reflective strips fitted on the rear of some vehicles may be red or yellow
qijoqk.why: Rear reflective strips may be red or yellow, while side strips are white or yellow.

2rtjkj.q: A driver who sees the panels shown is following a lorry with a laden mass above 3.5 tonnes
2rtjkj.why: Panels with diagonal yellow and red stripes identify the rear of a lorry (autocarro) with a maximum mass over 3.5 t.

117yee5.q: A driver who sees the panels shown is following a goods trailer or semi-trailer with a laden mass above 3.5 tonnes
117yee5.why: The yellow panel with a red border identifies the rear of a goods trailer or semi-trailer with a maximum mass over 3.5 t.

ca8dzt.q: Side reflective strips must be fitted on lorries with a maximum laden mass below 3.5 tonnes
ca8dzt.why: Reflective strips are compulsory for lorries and trailers with a maximum mass over 3.5 t, not for lighter ones.

1mjyl3f.q: When on the road, lorries with a maximum laden mass of 3.5 tonnes or less must be marked at the rear with yellow and red reflective panels
1mjyl3f.why: Yellow and red reflective rear panels are required only on lorries, trailers and semi-trailers with a maximum mass over 3.5 t.

1cl9t19.q: A sign showing the minimum permitted speed must be displayed on the rear of buses
1cl9t19.why: Buses and heavy vehicles carry a rear disc showing the maximum speed allowed for that vehicle, not a minimum speed.

1vgq3sv.q: A sign showing the maximum permitted speed must be displayed on the rear of cars
1vgq3sv.why: The rear maximum-speed disc is required on buses, heavy lorries and vehicles towing trailers, not on ordinary cars.

qssh6f.q: Caravans (roulottes) must be fitted at the rear with red or yellow reflective strips
qssh6f.why: Red or yellow rear reflective strips are required on goods lorries and trailers over 3.5 t, not on caravans.

1c50l8n.q: Buses must be fitted at the rear with red or white reflective strips
1c50l8n.why: Reflective strips are required on lorries and trailers over 3.5 t, not on buses; also, rear strips are red or yellow, never white.

1q065p9.q: The panel shown is fitted on the rear of trailers or semi-trailers with a laden mass above 3.5 tonnes
1q065p9.why: The diagonal yellow-and-red striped panel is for lorries over 3.5 t; trailers and semi-trailers use the yellow panel with a red border instead.

uaisxu.why: A motorcycle (motociclo) is a two-wheeled motor vehicle carrying the rider and possibly one passenger.

1c7axio.q: Motorcycles have an engine capacity above 50 cc
1c7axio.why: With a combustion engine, two-wheelers up to 50 cc and 45 km/h are mopeds (ciclomotori); above those limits they are motorcycles.

1iwjq2o.q: Mopeds (ciclomotori) do not fall into the motorcycle category
1iwjq2o.why: Mopeds (ciclomotori) are a separate category: up to 50 cc and 45 km/h, while motorcycles exceed those limits.

ll4hd3.q: Motorcycles may be fitted with an automatic gearbox
ll4hd3.why: The type of gearbox does not affect the classification: a motorcycle can have a manual or an automatic transmission.

qntf5j.q: Motorcycles must undergo a roadworthiness test (revisione) four years after first registration and every two years thereafter
qntf5j.why: Motorcycles have their first inspection (revisione) 4 years after first registration, then every 2 years.

w9yqgh.q: All three-wheeled motor vehicles are motorcycles
w9yqgh.why: Three-wheeled motor vehicles are tricycles (tricicli), a separate category from motorcycles, which always have two wheels.

gp1pyv.q: Motorcycles are motor vehicles with more than two wheels
gp1pyv.why: Motorcycles have exactly two wheels; with three wheels the vehicle is a tricycle (triciclo), with four a quadricycle (quadriciclo).

1xp1ier.q: A motorcycle is any two-wheeled vehicle
1xp1ier.why: Two wheels are not enough: bicycles and mopeds also have two wheels, but motorcycles must exceed 50 cc or 45 km/h.

1trwwhj.q: Only two-wheeled vehicles with an engine capacity up to 125 cc are defined as motorcycles
1trwwhj.why: There is no upper engine-size limit for motorcycles: up to 125 cc is just the light motorcycle class, ridable with an A1 licence.

ukiegw.q: Motorcycles have an engine capacity up to 50 cc and reach a speed of up to 45 km/h
ukiegw.why: Up to 50 cc and 45 km/h describes a moped (ciclomotore); motorcycles exceed 50 cc or 45 km/h.

ny1wis.q: For traffic purposes, light quadricycles are treated as motorcycles
ny1wis.why: Light quadricycles (quadricicli leggeri) are treated as mopeds, not motorcycles; heavier quadricycles are treated as motor vehicles of the motoveicolo class.

fa8gsn.q: Motor vehicles (autoveicoli) are motor vehicles with at least four wheels, excluding quadricycles
fa8gsn.why: Autoveicoli are motor vehicles with at least four wheels, excluding quadricycles, which are classed with motoveicoli or mopeds.

1jk7fp2.q: An autoveicolo is a motor vehicle with no fewer than four wheels, except quadricycles
1jk7fp2.why: An autoveicolo needs an engine and at least four wheels; quadricycles are excluded even though they have four wheels.

1yc7jeu.q: A bus is classed as an autoveicolo
1yc7jeu.why: A bus (autobus) is an autoveicolo designed to carry more than nine people, including the driver.

17gxkxk.why: A lorry (autocarro) is an autoveicolo designed to carry goods and the people who handle them.

1wjv31x.why: Although they have four wheels, quadricycles are not autoveicoli: light ones are treated as mopeds, the others as motoveicoli.

1dopqbd.q: Autoveicoli are all motor vehicles with four or more wheels, including quadricycles
1dopqbd.why: Autoveicoli are motor vehicles with at least four wheels, but quadricycles are expressly excluded.

1lalj2.q: Autoveicoli are all vehicles with at least two wheels
1lalj2.why: Autoveicoli must have an engine and at least four wheels; motor vehicles with two or three wheels are motoveicoli.

1xf4jzl.q: Autoveicoli are all vehicles with at least four wheels, including those without an engine
1xf4jzl.why: Autoveicoli are by definition motor vehicles; four-wheeled vehicles without an engine are, for example, trailers or hand carts.

1l5cb52.q: A motor tricycle is an autoveicolo
1l5cb52.why: A motor tricycle has three wheels and is a motoveicolo; autoveicoli have at least four wheels.

z5d6ef.q: An autoveicolo is any motor vehicle
z5d6ef.why: Not every motor vehicle is an autoveicolo: it needs at least four wheels and excludes quadricycles; mopeds and motoveicoli are separate categories.

smqx08.q: An autoveicolo is any vehicle used to carry goods
smqx08.why: An autoveicolo is defined by having an engine and at least four wheels, not by its use: it also includes cars and buses, which carry people.

12pnno6.q: A car (autovettura) is a four-wheeled motor vehicle designed to carry at most nine people, including the driver
12pnno6.why: A car (autovettura) is an autoveicolo for carrying people, with at most nine seats including the driver's.

18r4qf3.q: The car (autovettura) is one of the autoveicoli
18r4qf3.why: A car (autovettura) is one type of autoveicolo, alongside buses, lorries, road tractors and motorhomes.

q1ckg3.q: A car (autovettura) cannot have more than nine seats, including the driver's
q1ckg3.why: A car is limited to nine seats including the driver; with more seats the vehicle is a bus (autobus).

qfr7px.q: A bus is not a car (autovettura)
qfr7px.why: A bus carries more than nine people including the driver, while a car (autovettura) carries at most nine.

pyfua.q: Cars may have an electric motor
pyfua.why: The power source does not change the classification: a car can have a combustion, electric or hybrid engine.

196vahl.q: Cars are subject to periodic roadworthiness tests (revisione)
196vahl.why: Cars must have their first inspection (revisione) 4 years after first registration, then every 2 years.

oybuuf.q: All rear-wheel-drive motor vehicles are defined as cars (autovetture)
oybuuf.why: A car is defined by its use and seating (carrying people, nine seats at most including the driver), not by which wheels are driven.

1ecbhm7.q: Cars may not tow luggage trailers (carrelli-appendice) or trailers
1ecbhm7.why: Cars may tow a trailer or a light luggage trailer (carrello appendice), within the mass limits shown in the registration document.

lz5ltv.q: All vehicles with a front-mounted engine are defined as cars (autovetture)
lz5ltv.why: Engine position is irrelevant: a car is an autoveicolo for carrying people with at most nine seats including the driver.

10kucxp.q: A car (autovettura) is a vehicle with ten seats in total, including the driver's
10kucxp.why: A car has at most nine seats including the driver; a vehicle with ten seats is a bus (autobus).

dhr6pm.q: A car (autovettura) is defined as an armoured vehicle specially equipped for transporting valuables
dhr6pm.why: An armoured cash-transport vehicle is a special-purpose autoveicolo (trasporto specifico), not a car, which is meant to carry people.

w3eidp.why: A lorry (autocarro) is an autoveicolo for carrying goods, whereas a car (autovettura) is for carrying people.

1g0fznn.q: A car (autovettura) may have at most five seats
1g0fznn.why: A car may have up to nine seats including the driver, not just five.

1b21iw7.q: Cars are subject to a roadworthiness test (revisione) every five years
1b21iw7.why: Cars have their first inspection 4 years after first registration and then every 2 years, not every five.

19ky3kd.q: Trailers and semi-trailers are vehicles without an engine, designed to be towed
19ky3kd.why: Trailers and semi-trailers (rimorchi, semirimorchi) have no engine of their own and can only move when towed by a motor vehicle.

4ho369.q: Light trailers are those with a maximum laden mass of up to 750 kg
4ho369.why: A light trailer (rimorchio leggero) is one with a maximum laden mass of no more than 750 kg.

1xithf6.q: An articulated bus (autosnodato) is not classed as a trailer
1xithf6.why: An articulated bus (autosnodato) is made of two rigid sections joined by a pivot; it is a motor vehicle, not a trailer.

v1q2us.q: A motor caravan (autocaravan) is not a trailer
v1q2us.why: A motorhome (autocaravan) has its own engine and is an autoveicolo; the trailer version for accommodation is the caravan.

1n0b0kl.q: A caravan is not a trailer
1n0b0kl.why: A caravan is indeed a trailer: it has no engine, must be towed, and is fitted out as accommodation for use when parked.

1q46nkc.q: Light trailers are those with a maximum laden mass of up to 500 kg
1q46nkc.why: The limit for light trailers is a maximum laden mass of 750 kg, not 500 kg.

fopyf9.q: Semi-trailers are trailers without a braking system
fopyf9.why: Semi-trailers do have brakes; they differ from trailers because part of their weight rests on the towing tractor unit.

15q2c2n.q: Trailers are fitted with a silencer
15q2c2n.why: Trailers have no engine, so they have no exhaust or silencer; those belong to the towing vehicle.

eptegp.q: Junctions must be kept clear when traffic is heavy
eptegp.why: You must not enter a junction unless you are sure you can clear it, so you do not block cross traffic.

wk6pp3.q: Level crossings and tram tracks must be kept clear even when traffic is heavy
wk6pp3.why: Level crossings and tram tracks must always be kept clear: stopping on them in a queue is forbidden and very dangerous.

7rus3v.q: Pedestrian and cycle crossings must be kept clear when queues of vehicles form
7rus3v.why: When queuing you must stop before pedestrian and cycle crossings so pedestrians and cyclists can get across.

185gn03.q: Road entrances and exits (junctions, merges, car park entrances, etc.) must be kept clear even when traffic is heavy
185gn03.why: Even in heavy traffic you must keep junctions, merges and car park entrances clear so other vehicles can get in and out.

12k80k6.q: Only junctions controlled by traffic lights must be kept clear when queues of vehicles form
12k80k6.why: The duty to keep junctions clear applies to every intersection, with or without traffic lights, as well as to pedestrian and cycle crossings and level crossings.

aszfps.q: Overpasses must be kept clear in heavy traffic
aszfps.why: In queues you must keep junctions, level crossings, pedestrian and cycle crossings and side-road exits clear; overpasses (cavalcavia) are not among these places, so a queue can extend onto them.

t6om6s.q: Tunnels must be kept clear when queues of vehicles form
t6om6s.why: Tunnels (gallerie) are not among the places to keep clear in a queue; that duty applies to junctions, level crossings, pedestrian and cycle crossings and side-road exits. In a tunnel you simply stay in line, keeping your distance.

11wpvef.q: The entrances of private homes must be kept clear when queues of vehicles form
11wpvef.why: The queuing rule requires keeping junctions, level crossings, crossings and side-road exits clear, not the entrances of private houses.

1ai55o8.q: Underpasses must be kept clear in heavy traffic
1ai55o8.why: Underpasses (sottovia) are not among the places to keep clear in heavy traffic; those are junctions, level crossings, pedestrian and cycle crossings and side-road exits.

gr1v36.q: When travelling in a line of vehicles, you must not watch only the vehicle in front, but also look further ahead to monitor the traffic situation
gr1v36.why: Looking far ahead lets you spot slowdowns, obstacles or braking further up the line early and react smoothly, instead of relying only on the brake lights of the car in front.

1x5mwln.q: To help traffic flow, it is advisable to keep side-road exits clear when travelling behind a line of vehicles
1x5mwln.why: Stopping short of side-road exits in a queue lets vehicles enter or leave, avoiding blocking the junction and cross traffic.

1uj5mz.q: When travelling in a line of vehicles, you must still keep a safe distance
1uj5mz.why: Even in a line of traffic you must always keep a safe distance, because the vehicle ahead can brake suddenly and you need room to stop without hitting it.
