1eh4x4c.q: For greater safety, when travelling in a line of vehicles it is advisable not to get too close to the vehicle in front
1eh4x4c.why: Driving too close to the vehicle ahead cuts your stopping space and your view of the road, raising the risk of a rear-end collision if it brakes suddenly.

a47uj0.q: For greater safety, when travelling in a line of vehicles in built-up areas, it is advisable to always keep the hazard lights on
a47uj0.why: Hazard lights (luci di emergenza) are for a vehicle stopped in a dangerous position or to warn of a sudden slowdown or queue; they must not be kept on while driving in urban traffic.

1i15t1s.q: When travelling in a line of vehicles, you may let yourself be distracted if you are at low speed
1i15t1s.why: You must stay attentive at any speed: in a queue traffic stops and starts constantly, and a moment of distraction is enough to hit the vehicle in front.

hxbf3h.q: When travelling behind a line of vehicles, it is advisable to move as far left as possible to create a free lane on the right
hxbf3h.why: In a queue you stay in your own lane, keeping right; moving to the left to open a gap is wrong and dangerous, as it invades the space of overtaking or oncoming traffic.

ivasx9.q: When travelling in a line of vehicles, it is advisable to move to the centre of the carriageway to check the traffic situation
ivasx9.why: Even in a queue you must keep as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway (carreggiata); to check traffic you look far ahead, not move to the middle.

4glagc.q: Even in poor visibility, when travelling behind a vehicle that raises dust, it is best to overtake it immediately
4glagc.why: With poor visibility, such as behind a vehicle raising dust, overtaking is dangerous because you cannot see ahead: slow down, increase the distance and overtake only when the view is clear.

1u3cnvh.q: When entering a built-up area, you must bear in mind that right of way at junctions may change frequently
1u3cnvh.why: In built-up areas junctions are frequent and regulated in different ways (priority to the right, signs, traffic lights, officers), so right of way can change often from one junction to the next.

1hwgg8i.q: When entering a built-up area, you must bear in mind that the flow of traffic is often hindered or interrupted by vehicles that are stopped, pulling away or changing direction
1hwgg8i.why: Urban traffic is irregular: parked vehicles, vehicles pulling out, parking or turning often slow down or stop the flow, so constant attention is needed.

8idpz9.q: Once in a built-up area, you must bear in mind that other road users (such as pedestrians and cyclists) mix more with motor traffic
8idpz9.why: In built-up areas pedestrians, cyclists and other vulnerable users mix closely with motor traffic, so you must expect sudden crossings and movements.

18pz6rq.q: In a built-up area you must be more attentive, cautious and tolerant, because of the greater number of users interacting in the urban environment
18pz6rq.why: In urban areas the many different users (pedestrians, cyclists, motorcycles, buses) create more conflict situations, so greater attention, caution and tolerance are needed.

1wn357e.q: When entering a built-up area, you must keep concentrating on driving even though there may be more reasons to get distracted
1wn357e.why: In town there are more signs, shop windows, noise and movement that can distract you, but you must stay focused on driving because hazards are also more frequent.

jxuww7.q: When entering a built-up area, you must consider that parking is allowed at unregulated junctions
jxuww7.why: Parking is forbidden at junctions and within 5 metres of them (measured from the edge of the crossing carriageway), even when the junction is unregulated.

1bc9cq4.q: In a built-up area, driving in parallel lines is always allowed
1bc9cq4.why: In built-up areas driving in parallel lines (file parallele) is allowed only on carriageways with at least two lanes per direction, not always.

1udl0dy.q: In a built-up area, you must consider that pedestrians and people with disabilities must always give way to motor vehicles
1udl0dy.why: It is drivers who must give way to pedestrians on pedestrian crossings and stop for blind people with a white or white-and-red cane, even away from crossings.

hpnb5e.q: It is forbidden to move or deface road signs
hpnb5e.why: The Highway Code forbids moving, defacing, damaging or removing road signs (segnaletica stradale), since this would compromise their function and visibility.

1ctqukp.q: It is forbidden to remove road signs
1ctqukp.why: Removing road signs is forbidden: signs regulate traffic, and only the road authority may install or take them down.

ivz2pg.q: Moving road signs can create serious danger for other road users
ivz2pg.why: A moved sign may go unseen or give wrong information about where a hazard or rule applies, endangering other road users.

f0gqdt.q: Moving road signs is allowed if they are not danger signs
f0gqdt.why: The ban on moving road signs applies to all signs (danger, regulatory, informative and road markings), with no exceptions.

p39a8o.q: Moving road signs is allowed after notifying the police
p39a8o.why: Informing the police does not allow you to move signs; only the road authority or those it appoints may change road signage.

108hwtb.q: Moving road signs is allowed if they are delimitation barriers or traffic cones
108hwtb.why: Barriers and traffic cones are also road signage, often temporary for roadworks or accidents, and drivers must not move them.

qjh9r7.q: Speed racing on roads is forbidden
qjh9r7.why: Speed racing on roads is forbidden; motor sport events on public roads can take place only with authorisation and with the road closed to traffic.

1co5exa.q: A driver who takes part in unauthorised speed races in public areas is punished with imprisonment
1co5exa.why: Taking part in unauthorised speed races on public roads is a criminal offence (art. 9-ter), punished with imprisonment and a fine, plus licence suspension.

uy3a9b.q: A driver who races at speed on public roads is punished with imprisonment
uy3a9b.why: Racing on public roads without authorisation is a crime under art. 9-ter of the Highway Code, punished with imprisonment and a fine.

s75zci.q: Anyone who bets on vehicles taking part in unauthorised speed races on public roads is punished with imprisonment
s75zci.why: Art. 9-ter punishes with imprisonment and a fine not only organisers and participants but also anyone who bets on unauthorised speed races.

1jxocj9.q: Motor sport competitions in public areas are allowed without authorisation
1jxocj9.why: Motor sport competitions on public roads and areas always require authorisation from the competent authority; without it they are forbidden.

1qwr655.q: On public roads, speed races are allowed, even if unauthorised, from 23:00 to 06:00
1qwr655.why: Unauthorised races are forbidden at any time; there is no time window in which they are allowed.

1l9y58c.q: Speed races are allowed, even if unauthorised, provided only two cars take part
1l9y58c.why: The ban applies whatever the number of participants: even a race between just two cars is an unauthorised race and a criminal offence.

1fht1lb.q: On public roads, speed races are allowed, even if unauthorised, between motorcycles but not between motor vehicles
1fht1lb.why: The ban on unauthorised races covers every type of vehicle, motorcycles included, with no distinction by category.

14oypo4.q: It is forbidden to throw lit cigarette butts out of the window
14oypo4.why: Throwing objects from vehicles is forbidden, and lit cigarette butts are especially dangerous because they can hit other road users or start fires.

1kex2d8.q: Throwing lit cigarette butts out of the window is very dangerous, especially if two-wheeled vehicles are coming up behind
1kex2d8.why: A lit butt can hit motorcyclists or cyclists, who have no bodywork protecting them, distracting or burning them and causing falls.

glbqmc.q: Throwing lit cigarette butts out of the window near woods or green areas could cause fires
glbqmc.why: Near woods and green areas, especially with dry vegetation, a lit cigarette butt can start a fire.

azn1vf.q: It is forbidden to spread mud or debris on the road with a vehicle's dirty wheels
azn1vf.why: The Highway Code forbids dirtying the road with mud or debris carried by the wheels, as they make the surface slippery and dangerous for others.

1f4qi3m.q: A driver who notices that their vehicle is leaking oil must take all necessary action to avoid danger to other users
1f4qi3m.why: Oil on the carriageway makes it very slippery, especially for two-wheelers; a driver whose vehicle leaks oil must stop, limit the leak and warn of the danger.

1sob135.q: A driver who notices that their vehicle has heavy oil or fuel leaks must immediately notify the road owner authority or the police
1sob135.why: With heavy oil or fuel leaks the driver must promptly inform the road authority or the police so the carriageway can be signposted and cleaned.

1dhank4.q: The driver of a two-wheeled vehicle may carry a pet, if kept in a suitable cage, provided it does not stick out by more than 50 centimetres.
1dhank4.why: On two-wheelers a pet may be carried in a suitable cage or carrier, provided it is secured and does not stick out more than 50 cm sideways or beyond the vehicle's outline.

m6dl3x.q: When driving a vehicle, the driver must go over puddles at low speed
m6dl3x.why: Driving slowly through puddles avoids splashing pedestrians and other users and reduces the risk of aquaplaning and loss of grip.

uc3his.q: If, when leaving a muddy track, you make the road considerably dirty, you may incur an administrative fine
uc3his.why: Dirtying the road with mud or soil is forbidden by the Highway Code and punished with an administrative fine, plus the duty to clean it up.

1orw2pv.q: To avoid dirtying the carriageway, you must clean the vehicle's wheels before leaving a muddy track
1orw2pv.why: Cleaning the wheels before joining the road avoids spreading mud on the carriageway, which would make it slippery and is an offence.

1jf2lrn.q: When leaving a muddy track or a building site, you must make sure that no soil falls off while driving and dirties the road
1jf2lrn.why: The driver must prevent soil, mud or debris from falling onto the road, since they endanger others and dirtying the carriageway is forbidden.

1sndvib.q: It is allowed to move temporary vertical road signs in order to park the vehicle
1sndvib.why: Temporary signs, such as roadworks or temporary no-parking signs, must not be moved either; to park you must find a permitted space.

1vozm8v.q: It is allowed to throw paper out of the window
1vozm8v.why: Throwing any object from a vehicle, paper included, is forbidden: it litters the road and can distract or hit other users.

bwvb9l.q: The driver may throw objects out of the window onto the hard shoulder
bwvb9l.why: The ban on throwing objects applies to the whole road, including the hard shoulder (banchina), which is part of the road and used by pedestrians and stopped vehicles.

1xx47g9.q: On a road covered with loose gravel, the driver may drive at high speed
1xx47g9.why: On loose gravel (brecciolino) grip is reduced and the tyres throw stones at other vehicles and pedestrians, so you must drive at moderate speed.

fgtjhs.q: The driver may overtake queuing vehicles by accelerating sharply and repeatedly changing lanes
fgtjhs.why: Sudden acceleration and repeated lane-changing in a queue is dangerous and incorrect: it raises the risk of collisions, and you must stay in line in your lane.

10o964.q: The driver of a vehicle, besides obeying the specific traffic rules, must behave correctly and tolerantly towards other road users
10o964.why: Besides the rules, drivers must behave so as not to cause danger or obstruction, showing correctness and tolerance towards other road users.

1qqjsts.q: When approaching a junction, the driver must always use the utmost caution, even when the other drivers must give way to them
1qqjsts.why: Having right of way does not guarantee others will respect it: approaching a junction you must always moderate speed and be ready to stop.

acd923.q: The driver of a vehicle must protect their own safety and that of others
acd923.why: Drivers are responsible not only for their own safety but also for that of their passengers and all other road users.

1llas9d.q: The driver of a vehicle must respect traffic officers and cooperate with them
1llas9d.why: Traffic officers direct traffic and their signals override traffic lights and signs; drivers must respect them and follow their instructions.

lf2ksn.q: The driver of a vehicle must try to anticipate the behaviour of other road users
lf2ksn.why: Anticipating others, such as a pedestrian about to cross or a car that may turn, lets you react in time and avoid accidents.

gczsrr.q: The driver of a vehicle must be patient and tolerant even when traffic slows down
gczsrr.why: In slow traffic impatience leads to risky manoeuvres and aggressive behaviour; staying calm and tolerant reduces danger for everyone.

8h22ir.q: The driver of a vehicle must not always rely on the behaviour of others, which may not be correct
8h22ir.why: Other users can make mistakes or break the rules, for example by not giving way, so you must drive defensively and be ready to react.

1mujd3r.q: The driver of a vehicle cannot insist on going first when there is doubt that they will be given right of way
1mujd3r.why: If you doubt the other driver will give way, you must slow down or stop: insisting on your right of way can cause a crash.

1fl8mvf.q: Having right of way does not authorise the driver to cross the junction without caution
1fl8mvf.why: Even with right of way you must cross the junction carefully and at moderate speed, checking that others are actually stopping.

7kj56q.q: The driver of a large vehicle normally has right of way over the driver of a smaller vehicle
7kj56q.why: Right of way does not depend on vehicle size but on junction rules and signs, such as priority to the right or give-way and stop signs.

a3qn3a.q: The driver of a vehicle may take advantage of their vehicle's power to avoid giving way to those entitled to it
a3qn3a.why: A vehicle's power gives no rights: right of way must be given to whoever is entitled to it under the rules and signs.

15gpg7e.q: The driver of a heavy vehicle may behave in a way that causes annoyance to others
15gpg7e.why: Every driver, including of heavy vehicles, must behave correctly and respectfully, without intimidating or annoying other road users.

b2u9yv.q: The driver of a vehicle must respect traffic officers only if they are in uniform
b2u9yv.why: Traffic officers' instructions must always be obeyed, even when they are not in uniform but are recognisable, for example by a badge or signalling disc (paletta).

nuci3.q: The driver of a vehicle can do without the utmost caution when approaching a junction where they have right of way
nuci3.why: Even with right of way you must approach the junction with maximum caution, because others may not respect it.

ygsusq.q: The driver must show signs of impatience if the vehicle in front is going too slowly
ygsusq.why: Showing impatience with the horn, flashing lights or tailgating is wrong and dangerous; if the vehicle ahead is slow, wait or overtake when it is safe.

19sqa60.q: An accident, even at low speed, could cause serious physical harm to pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists, if involved
19sqa60.why: Pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists have no bodywork to protect them, so even a low-speed impact can cause them serious injuries.

fix7ju.q: You must frequently check the rear-view mirror for approaching cyclists or motorcyclists
fix7ju.why: Cyclists and motorcyclists are small, quick and easy to miss, so you must check your mirrors often, especially before turning or changing lanes.

r7ymay.q: After parking the vehicle at the side of the carriageway, the driver must check that no cyclists or motorcyclists are approaching before opening the door
r7ymay.why: Before opening the door you must check the mirrors and look round for approaching cyclists or motorcyclists, so as not to cause danger or obstruction.

oqs74u.q: The interior pillars of motor vehicles affect visibility
oqs74u.why: The pillars (montanti) supporting the roof create blind spots where pedestrians, bicycles or motorcycles can disappear, especially at bends and junctions.

oqggcj.q: The interior pillars of motor vehicles reduce the chance of seeing a cyclist or motorcyclist
oqggcj.why: A cyclist or motorcyclist, being narrow, can be hidden behind a roof pillar, so at junctions you should move your head to check properly.

q8pnxv.q: A low-speed accident does not create safety problems for the drivers involved
q8pnxv.why: Even at low speed a collision can cause injuries, such as whiplash, especially without seat belts or with badly adjusted head restraints.

1jvtvqx.q: A driver getting out of a parked vehicle does not need to check for approaching cyclists
1jvtvqx.why: Before opening the door and getting out you must check for approaching cyclists or other vehicles, as an opening door can knock them down.

1g63quq.q: In the rear-view mirror, the driver must check only for approaching lorries or buses
1g63quq.why: In the mirrors you must watch for every approaching user, especially cyclists and motorcyclists, who are the hardest to see.

f29xl7.q: A motorcycle rider may weave between vehicles stopped at a traffic light
f29xl7.why: Weaving between vehicles stopped at traffic lights is dangerous and incorrect: motorcyclists too must stay in line in their lane.

42v0os.q: A motorcycle rider may park on the pavement even where there are no designated parking spaces
42v0os.why: The pavement (marciapiede) is reserved for pedestrians: motorcycles may park on it only in specifically marked spaces.

1o8ke7z.q: A motorcycle rider may ride on the pavement if traffic on the carriageway is blocked
1o8ke7z.why: Motor vehicles may never ride on the pavement (marciapiede), even when traffic is blocked, because it is reserved for pedestrians.

14wztqp.q: Greater caution must be used towards people with disabilities
14wztqp.why: People with disabilities may move more slowly or have difficulty perceiving vehicles, so they call for more attention and readiness to stop.

1yrfef9.q: Greater caution must be used towards elderly people
1yrfef9.why: Elderly people may have slower reflexes, less mobility and reduced ability to judge vehicle speed and distance, so extra caution is needed.

1nshvxp.q: Greater caution must be used towards children crossing the road
1nshvxp.why: Children are unpredictable, hard to see because of their height and cannot judge traffic dangers, so you must slow down and be ready to stop.

73yglr.q: Greater caution must be used towards drivers who show uncertain driving
73yglr.why: Drivers who seem unsure, such as beginners, may make sudden or wrong manoeuvres; increase your distance and be ready to react.

1ct62p8.q: Greater caution must be used towards drivers of vehicles adapted for people with disabilities
1ct62p8.why: Drivers of vehicles adapted for people with disabilities may have different reaction times or ways of manoeuvring, so greater caution is needed around them.

1a7tmrb.q: Greater caution must be used towards people on bicycles and those with limited mobility
1a7tmrb.why: Cyclists and people with limited mobility are vulnerable users: little protected, slow or unsteady, they need more space and attention.

1vll3sp.q: Particular caution must be used towards drivers who obtained their driving licence in a foreign country
1vll3sp.why: Holding a foreign licence does not in itself mean unsafe driving: no special caution is required for this category of drivers.

cuuo5r.q: Greater caution must be used towards drivers of electric motor vehicles
cuuo5r.why: The type of propulsion does not call for special caution towards the driver; if anything, quiet electric vehicles require attention from pedestrians.

dfctw6.q: Greater caution must be used towards taxi drivers
dfctw6.why: Taxi drivers are not a category for which special caution is required; extra caution applies to vulnerable users such as children, the elderly and the disabled.

13zm5eg.q: Greater caution must be used towards drivers of motor tricycles
13zm5eg.why: Motor tricycles (tricicli a motore) do not call for special caution compared with other vehicles; extra caution is owed to vulnerable users.

173cnsc.q: Greater caution must be used towards pedestrians carrying a white cane, but not towards those with a white-and-red cane
173cnsc.why: A white-and-red cane identifies a deafblind person, who is even more vulnerable; drivers must stop and take maximum care with both white and white-and-red canes.

438jof.q: When elderly people cross the carriageway, you must bear in mind that they may not pay adequate attention to vehicles
438jof.why: Elderly people may misjudge vehicles' speed and distance or not notice them due to sight or hearing problems, so you must be ready to stop.

cb64b.q: When elderly people cross the carriageway, you must bear in mind that they might stop suddenly in the middle of the road
cb64b.why: Elderly pedestrians may hesitate, tire or lose confidence halfway across and stop suddenly in the middle of the carriageway (carreggiata), so drive slowly and expect it.

rpb2be.q: When elderly people cross the carriageway, you must bear in mind that they might not look either right or left
rpb2be.why: With age, attention, eyesight and neck mobility decline, so an elderly person may cross without checking traffic either way; the driver must be ready to stop.

1x34ue1.q: When elderly people cross the carriageway, you must bear in mind that, given their age, they do not react promptly to dangerous situations
1x34ue1.why: Older people have slower reflexes and react late to danger, so it is up to the driver to slow down and keep a safety margin.

90jft2.q: When elderly people cross the carriageway, you must not get too close with your vehicle, to avoid them feeling threatened and reacting with dangerous movements
90jft2.why: A vehicle that comes too close can frighten an elderly pedestrian into sudden moves such as stepping back or falling; stop at a respectful distance and let them cross calmly.

1meinpf.q: Elderly people crossing the carriageway are exposed to greater dangers, because their eyesight and hearing are no longer excellent
1meinpf.why: Weaker eyesight and hearing mean an elderly pedestrian may not see or hear an approaching vehicle, which puts them at greater risk when crossing.

2xa1qx.q: Elderly people crossing the carriageway are exposed to greater dangers, because they might misjudge the speed of approaching vehicles
2xa1qx.why: Judging the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles gets harder with age, so an elderly pedestrian may think there is enough time to cross when there is not.

19glj08.q: When elderly people cross the carriageway, you must bear in mind that they have quicker reflexes and therefore cross more carefully
19glj08.why: Older people have slower, not faster, reflexes: they cross slowly and react late to danger, so they call for extra caution.

g8ybv3.q: When elderly people cross the carriageway, you must bear in mind that they usually cross quickly and cautiously
g8ybv3.why: Elderly pedestrians usually cross slowly and sometimes hesitantly or inattentively, so the driver must give them all the time they need.

vtpgye.q: When elderly people cross the carriageway, you must bear in mind that, having more experience and a wider field of vision, they sense dangerous situations better
vtpgye.why: With age the field of vision narrows and hazard perception worsens; experience does not make up for reduced physical and sensory sharpness.

15ljr36.q: When elderly people cross the carriageway, you must flash your headlights and sound the horn to make them cross quickly
15ljr36.why: Horns and flashing lights can frighten an elderly pedestrian into dangerous reactions; instead, stop and wait patiently until they have finished crossing.

1kfewtl.q: When elderly people cross the carriageway, you must give way only to those crossing from left to right
1kfewtl.why: Pedestrians on a crossing must be given way whichever direction they are walking in, and elderly people deserve even more caution.

17sma8p.q: The driver must stop and give way to a blind pedestrian with a white cane who is about to cross the road away from the zebra crossing
17sma8p.why: A white cane (bastone bianco) identifies a blind pedestrian; the driver must stop and give way even when they cross away from a zebra crossing (art. 191 of the Highway Code).

1m1oaus.q: The driver must stop and make it easier for a blind pedestrian with a white cane to cross the road away from the zebra crossing
1m1oaus.why: When a blind pedestrian with a white cane crosses, the driver must stop and make the crossing easier for them, wherever they cross, even away from the stripes.

13l5h2r.q: The driver must give way to a blind pedestrian with a white cane crossing the road away from the zebra crossing, even if they are not accompanied by a guide dog
13l5h2r.why: The duty to give way applies because of the white cane itself; a guide dog is another sign of blindness, but both do not need to be present.

xio9oc.q: The driver must stop to give way to a deafblind pedestrian who, with a red-and-white cane, is crossing the road away from the zebra crossing
xio9oc.why: A white-and-red cane (bastone bianco-rosso) marks a deafblind person, who is protected like a blind pedestrian: stop and give way even away from a crossing.

831472.q: The driver must give way to a pedestrian with a white or red-and-white cane crossing the road, even if they are away from the stripes of a pedestrian crossing
831472.why: Both the white cane (blind) and the white-and-red cane (deafblind) require the driver to stop and give way, whether or not the person is on a zebra crossing.

16yj2lc.q: The driver must stop when a blind pedestrian with a white cane is about to cross the road, avoiding braking sharply so as not to frighten them
16yj2lc.why: A blind pedestrian relies on hearing, so a sudden screech of brakes can startle and disorient them; slow down early and stop smoothly.

145y0qa.q: The driver must accelerate to clear the carriageway quickly when a blind pedestrian with a white cane crosses the road without a guide dog
145y0qa.why: You must stop and let the white-cane pedestrian cross, with or without a guide dog; speeding up is dangerous and breaks the duty to give way.

1yuywgc.q: The driver must go first, since they have right of way, when a blind pedestrian with a white cane crosses the road away from the zebra crossing
1yuywgc.why: The pedestrian with a white cane has priority even away from the zebra crossing; the driver must stop and let them pass.

eyorl5.q: When a blind pedestrian with a white cane crosses the road away from the zebra crossing, the driver must give way only if the pedestrian crossing is more than 100 metres away
eyorl5.why: There is no distance condition: a white-cane pedestrian always gets priority, wherever they cross and however far they are from a zebra crossing.

1cofym.q: The driver must give way to a blind pedestrian crossing the road away from the zebra crossing only if they carry a red-and-white cane
1cofym.why: The duty applies to both the white cane (blind) and the white-and-red cane (deafblind), not only to the latter.

1rcxvwq.q: The driver must expect a blind pedestrian with a white cane crossing the road away from the zebra crossing to walk quickly and without hesitation
1rcxvwq.why: A blind pedestrian usually moves carefully and may hesitate, so the driver should expect a slow crossing and wait patiently.

ti3gdc.q: If a pedestrian with a white cane crosses the road away from the zebra crossing, you must sound the horn to urge them to cross quickly
ti3gdc.why: The horn can startle and disorient someone who cannot see; stop quietly and let them cross at their own pace.

1lbs7wt.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that a pedestrian crossing the road may become unsure and suddenly turn back
1lbs7wt.why: A pedestrian may hesitate midway and suddenly turn back, so when approaching a crossing slow down and be ready to stop.

1415qvq.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that elderly people usually cross slowly and with difficulty
1415qvq.why: Elderly people often walk slowly and with difficulty, so give them all the time they need to finish crossing at the zebra crossing.

1o4ykrv.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that the reactions of children crossing are unpredictable and can therefore create danger
1o4ykrv.why: Children are impulsive and not fully aware of danger; they may run, stop or change direction suddenly, so take maximum care near a crossing.

1kvax2b.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that children might step onto the stripes and then suddenly turn back for no apparent reason
1kvax2b.why: Children may start across and then dart back for no obvious reason; the driver must slow down and anticipate it.

w9xy0b.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that a pedestrian might stop suddenly on the stripes of the pedestrian crossing
w9xy0b.why: A pedestrian may freeze on the crossing through uncertainty or distraction, so approach slowly and stay able to stop.

lu8qqt.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that pedestrians, especially children, may suddenly appear from between parked vehicles
lu8qqt.why: Parked vehicles hide pedestrians, especially small children, who may step out suddenly into the carriageway (carreggiata), so proceed with care.

ubchaz.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that vehicles parked close to the stripes block the view of pedestrians
ubchaz.why: Cars parked near a crossing block the view between pedestrians and drivers, which is also why parking on or close to crossings is forbidden.

6kjhfx.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must expect children to react quickly and behave correctly
6kjhfx.why: Expect unpredictable and sometimes wrong behaviour from children, not quick correct reactions; the driver must be ready to stop.

1gcw9kr.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, pedestrians must signal with their hand before starting to cross
1gcw9kr.why: No rule requires pedestrians to signal with a hand; it is the driver who must give way to anyone crossing or about to cross on the stripes.

my8bup.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that a pedestrian with a white cane has more experience in how to cross the carriageway
my8bup.why: A white cane signals a blind person, who is especially vulnerable; the driver must stop and take the utmost care.

jzv2kp.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must stop if the crossing pedestrian has a red-and-white cane, but need only slow down if they have a white cane
jzv2kp.why: You must stop and give way in both cases: the white cane (blind) and the white-and-red cane (deafblind) get the same protection.

1jz3xc4.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must accelerate just enough to pass in front of the crossing pedestrian
1jz3xc4.why: A pedestrian on a crossing must be given way by slowing and, if needed, stopping; speeding up to pass in front of them is forbidden and dangerous.

7eblj0.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that if a pedestrian has stopped in the middle of the crossing stripes, it means they have given up their right to cross
7eblj0.why: A pedestrian who has stopped on the crossing still has priority; they may have frozen and could move again at any moment, so wait.

5mo1s3.q: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that pedestrians must cross the road side by side, so as to take less time
5mo1s3.why: No rule says pedestrians must cross side by side; they must cross carefully, and the driver must give way however they do it.

n516p8.q: When there are children waiting at a traffic light, you must be careful, because they might suddenly cross the road as soon as the vehicle light changes from green to yellow
n516p8.why: When the traffic light for vehicles turns amber, children may think they can go and run into the road; anticipate this and proceed carefully.

3igq0m.q: When there are children waiting at a traffic light, you must be careful, because they might quickly cross the road even on red, thinking it lasts too long
3igq0m.why: Impatient and impulsive, children may run across even on a red pedestrian light, so the driver must stay alert even on green.

198fkoi.q: When there are children waiting at a traffic light, you must be careful, because they may push one another and end up on the carriageway
198fkoi.why: In groups children play and push each other, and one may end up in the carriageway (carreggiata), so take care near a light where children are waiting.

ud84h8.q: When there are children waiting at a traffic light, you must be careful, because they might step off the pavement onto the carriageway while their light is still red
ud84h8.why: Children may step off the pavement (marciapiede) into the carriageway before their pedestrian light turns green; the driver must be ready to brake.

u0mv8m.q: Before entering a junction after the traffic light has turned green, the driver must wait for pedestrians to finish crossing the road
u0mv8m.why: Even on green, the driver must let pedestrians still in the carriageway finish crossing before entering the junction.

1tjsf1y.q: When there are children waiting at a traffic light, you must bear in mind that they may cross the road only if accompanied by an adult
1tjsf1y.why: No rule forbids children from crossing alone; the driver must always expect them to do so, even without an adult.

p4ieg0.q: At a traffic light, children may cross the road only after receiving a gesture of consent from drivers
p4ieg0.why: At traffic lights pedestrians cross according to the pedestrian signal, not because a driver waves them on; drivers have no authority to permit crossing.

9c73qu.q: When there are children waiting at a traffic light, you can be sure they will cross the road only when the pedestrian light shows green
9c73qu.why: You can never be sure how children will behave; they may cross even on a red pedestrian light, so always be careful.

emi05u.q: When there are children waiting at a traffic light, you can be sure they will not cross the road if the traffic light is flashing yellow
emi05u.why: A flashing amber light does not stop pedestrians and calls for caution; children may cross at any moment, so there is no certainty at all.

wyzp5c.q: When driving near a bus stop lay-by for a bus carrying schoolchildren, watch out for children who might have started crossing the carriageway hidden by the bus
wyzp5c.why: A stopped bus blocks the view; children who get off may cross in front of or behind it and appear suddenly in the carriageway (carreggiata).

6jveae.q: When driving near a lay-by for a school bus stop, watch out for children, who might run across the road to get on the school bus
6jveae.why: Children running late may dash across the road to catch the school bus without looking, so slow down near the stop.

10codjf.q: When driving near a lay-by for a school bus stop, you must be ready to brake in case children suddenly cross the road
10codjf.why: Near a school bus stop, reduce speed and be ready to brake, because children may suddenly cross.

1o75mua.q: When driving near a lay-by for a school bus stop, you must be careful and take into account children's unpredictable behaviour
1o75mua.why: Children behave unpredictably, especially in groups getting on or off the school bus, so the driver must proceed with particular caution.

5fmqtv.q: Near a lay-by for a school bus stop, children may get off the bus without paying attention to approaching vehicles
5fmqtv.why: When getting off the school bus, children may run straight into the road without checking traffic; approaching drivers must expect this and slow down.

685lsf.q: When driving near a lay-by for a school bus stop, you must slow down particularly if the school bus is there
685lsf.why: A school bus at the stop means children getting on, off or crossing, often hidden by the bus, so slow down considerably.

12idnyo.q: When driving near a lay-by for a school bus stop, you must not slow down, to avoid obstructing other traffic
12idnyo.why: Children's safety comes before traffic flow: near a school bus stop you must slow down.

1gl31b1.q: When driving near a lay-by for a school bus stop, you must go first, as you always have right of way over children crossing the road
1gl31b1.why: The driver has no priority over children crossing the road; they must slow down and, if necessary, stop to let them pass.

15ilrvi.q: When driving near a lay-by for a school bus stop, you must sound the horn to invite children crossing on the zebra crossing to give way
15ilrvi.why: On a zebra crossing pedestrians, children included, have priority; honking would frighten them and could cause dangerous reactions.

19c78kg.q: When driving near a lay-by for a school bus stop, you must slow down only if there are children crossing
19c78kg.why: You must slow down anyway, because children may suddenly appear from behind the bus or run towards it, even if nobody is crossing yet.

suvj0h.q: When driving near a lay-by for a school bus stop, watch out for the school bus, which will certainly reverse after stopping
suvj0h.why: When leaving the stop, the school bus normally pulls back into traffic rather than reversing; the real hazard is children crossing.

10k1kcf.q: When driving near a lay-by for a school bus stop, you may not continue driving if the school bus doors are still open
10k1kcf.why: No rule forbids passing while the school bus doors are open; you may proceed, but slowly and ready to stop for children.

160h5xj.q: When driving near a lay-by for a school bus stop, there is no need to slow down if the school bus is stationary
160h5xj.why: A stopped school bus is exactly the riskiest moment, as children get on, off and cross hidden by the bus, so you must slow down.

1wx9na3.q: Near a taxi rank, the driver must slow down and if necessary stop if pedestrians are crossing the road without looking
1wx9na3.why: Near a taxi rank, pedestrians often hurry across without looking to reach a cab, so slow down and be ready to stop.

m8qqtt.q: Near a taxi rank, the driver must watch out for pedestrians getting into or out of taxis
m8qqtt.why: People getting in or out of taxis may open doors or step into the carriageway (carreggiata) suddenly, so pay attention.

xibjfu.q: The driver of a vehicle other than a taxi may not park in spaces reserved for taxis
xibjfu.why: Taxi ranks are reserved exclusively for taxis; all other vehicles are forbidden to park there (art. 158 of the Highway Code).

1fhqwax.q: Near a taxi rank, the driver must watch out for pedestrians, who may suddenly cross the road without due care
1fhqwax.why: Pedestrians heading for a taxi or just out of one may cross abruptly without proper care; the driver must expect this and slow down.

tgujrd.q: Near a taxi rank, the driver must give way to taxis entering the road
tgujrd.why: A taxi leaving the rank is joining traffic and must give way to passing vehicles, just like any other vehicle.

1wsdlda.q: Near a taxi rank, the driver must give way to departing taxis if they enter from the left side of the carriageway
1wsdlda.why: Anyone pulling out of a parking area into traffic must give way to moving vehicles, whichever side of the carriageway they start from.

tbgjhh.q: The driver of a vehicle other than a taxi may park in spaces reserved for taxis from 20:00 to 08:00
tbgjhh.why: The ban on parking in taxi ranks applies at all hours, unless a supplementary sign states otherwise.

kiliet.q: When the carriageway is occupied by cyclists or pedestrians, it is prudent to keep an adequate lateral safety distance when overtaking them
kiliet.why: When overtaking cyclists or pedestrians, leave plenty of side room because they may move or wobble suddenly; for bicycles the law asks for at least 1.5 m where possible.

1bs17jd.q: When the carriageway is occupied by cyclists or pedestrians, it is not prudent to overtake them if a sufficient lateral distance cannot be kept.
1bs17jd.why: If there is not enough room for a safe side gap, stay behind and wait until overtaking can be done safely.

1nwr9ow.q: When an out-of-town carriageway is occupied by cyclists or pedestrians, it is advisable to sound the horn before overtaking them
1nwr9ow.why: Outside built-up areas the horn may be used to warn of your presence when safety requires it, for example alerting cyclists or pedestrians before overtaking them.

1f4ds1m.q: A driver intending to overtake cyclists or pedestrians occupying the carriageway must be very careful
1f4ds1m.why: Cyclists and pedestrians are vulnerable road users who may move suddenly, so overtake at moderate speed with a wide side gap.

hz0btu.q: Since cyclists sometimes wobble slightly as they ride, a driver must take this into account when overtaking
hz0btu.why: Potholes, wind or fatigue can make a cyclist wobble, so leave enough side clearance when overtaking to allow for it.

1hfcqlt.q: A driver intending to overtake cyclists or pedestrians occupying the carriageway must keep a lateral distance of at least 2 metres
1hfcqlt.why: The rule does not set 2 metres: it requires an adequate side gap and, when overtaking bicycles, at least 1.5 m where road conditions allow.

1wz4sk4.q: It is forbidden to overtake cyclists or pedestrians occupying the carriageway
1wz4sk4.why: Overtaking cyclists and pedestrians is allowed, as long as it is done carefully, at moderate speed and with a safe side gap.

d3ammq.q: At night, the driver does not have to give way to pedestrians crossing on the zebra crossing
d3ammq.why: The duty to give way to pedestrians on zebra crossings applies at all hours; at night, with poor visibility, even more care is needed.

1619u8i.q: When the carriageway is occupied by cyclists or pedestrians, they must be overtaken without exceeding 30 km/h
1619u8i.why: There is no fixed 30 km/h limit for this overtaking; speed must suit the situation while keeping a wide side gap.

q4gb1s.q: The driver must allow a pregnant woman to cross the road without hurrying her
q4gb1s.why: A pregnant woman may move more slowly and less nimbly; the driver must stop and let her cross calmly, without rushing her.

12sk87z.q: Greater care must be taken with pregnant women crossing the road
12sk87z.why: Pregnant women are less agile and cannot dodge quickly, so take extra care when they are crossing.

1smsk09.q: Greater care must be taken with pedestrians pushing a baby pram
1smsk09.why: A pram sticks out in front of the person pushing it and may appear first between cars, and the pedestrian moves more slowly, so take extra care.

ejd9ua.q: When parking a vehicle, it is forbidden to block any kerb ramps, so as not to prevent pedestrians pushing a baby pram from getting through
ejd9ua.why: Kerb ramps are there for prams and people with disabilities; parking in front of them or blocking them is forbidden (art. 158 of the Highway Code).

p90978.q: When a pregnant woman is crossing the carriageway, you must not get too close with your vehicle, to avoid frightening her
p90978.why: A vehicle that comes too close may frighten a pregnant woman into sudden moves or a fall, so stop at a suitable distance.

lfu4jq.q: When a pregnant woman is crossing the carriageway, you must bear in mind that she walks faster and therefore crosses quickly
lfu4jq.why: During pregnancy walking is usually slower and more careful, so the driver should allow more time for crossing.

9mvxvs.q: When a pedestrian pushing a baby pram is crossing the carriageway, you must bear in mind that they usually cross quickly
9mvxvs.why: Someone pushing a pram usually crosses slowly, also because of kerbs to negotiate, so give them all the time they need.

16umsg1.q: It is permitted to park a vehicle in front of kerb ramps only from 22:00 to 08:00
16umsg1.why: The ban on parking in front of kerb ramps applies at all hours, because passage for prams and disabled people must always be guaranteed.

n16a8n.q: When a pregnant woman is crossing the carriageway, you must give way to her only if she is crossing from left to right
n16a8n.why: Pedestrians on a crossing have priority whichever direction they walk in, and pregnant women deserve even more care.

1xi5845.q: When a pedestrian pushing a baby pram is crossing the carriageway, you must give way to them only if they are crossing from left to right
1xi5845.why: A pedestrian with a pram on a crossing must be given way in either direction, with particular care.

5ka53y.q: It is permitted to leave a vehicle parked on the pavement without leaving room for pedestrians pushing a baby pram
5ka53y.why: Parking on the pavement (marciapiede) is forbidden unless signs allow it; even then, enough room must be left for pedestrians, prams included.
